Select Board
Monday, March 30, 2026
6:00pm
Board Members Present: Tara White
Bill West
Beth Dean
Others Present: Mari Enoch, Town Administrator
Jennifer Greenberg, Admin. Secretary
Barbara Flach
Brad Sanzenbacher
Present on Zoom: Doug Newman
Beth Dean called the meeting to order at 6:01pm and announced the meeting is being recorded.
Pledge of Allegiance and Moment of Silence for Veterans
The Pledge of Allegiance was recited and a moment of silence for Veterans was held.
Updates on Farmer’s Market and request to revisit location—Barbara Flach
The Select Board provided feedback on the list of rules Barbara prepared for the Farmer’s
Market. She will ask vendors who have established businesses to provide their insurance
information. Mari requested she provide copies to the Town. Other vendors will fill out a waiver.
The Board approved holding the Farmer’s Market on the Town Green, and asked that vehicles be
discouraged from parking on the Green unless required for mobility reasons. Tara suggested
Barbara speak with the Meeting House about access to electricity. Barbara plans to utilize social
media to publicize the market.
Here resident complaint about road conditions on Cross Road to Canaan Valley Road
Brad Sanzenbacher lives in one of three homes on Cross to Canaan Valley Rd. near Konkapot
Rd. He said this dirt road has not been maintained by the Town for many years, and requested
1
that the road be added back into the maintenance schedule to prevent hazardous conditions. Mari
said Highway Superintendent Chuck Loring intends to add gravel and grade the road up to the
last of the three houses. Beyond that point, he will not be maintaining the road. The Board
agreed that signage alerting motorists that the road will not be maintained past the last house is
needed.
Here and act on request from Town Clerk to opt out of Early Voting by mail for May 11 Annual
Election
Because there is a high cost in both time and postage, the Town Clerk has requested that New
Marlborough opt out of early voting for the local election in May. Though towns are required to
hold early voting for all state and national elections, early voting for local elections is optional.
The Board of Registrars has already opted out of early voting in person. It is the Select Board’s
decision to opt out of early voting by mail.
Beth made a motion, Tara seconded, and it was so voted to opt out of early voting by mail
for the May 11th Annual Election per the Town Clerk’s request.
Bill West Aye
Tara B. White Aye
Beth Dean Aye
Town Administrator Updates
Mari Enoch said that Leisl Carlson resigned from the Cultural Council.
Although the timing of the school budget is unclear, Mari said she hopes to finalize the Town
side of the budget soon.
A walkthrough for firms interested in responding to the Town Hall Renovation Request for
Proposals (RFQ) will take place on Wednesday, April 1st at 10 am.
Select Board Updates
None.
Administrative: Payroll and Vendor Warrants, Business Licenses
Payroll and vendor warrants were signed.
Review and approve minutes of previous meetings
None.

Doug Newman asked for a recap of the discussion about the Farmer’s Market.
Adjourn
2
Being that there was no further business to be brought before the Board, a motion was
made by Beth, seconded by Tara, and it was so voted to adjourn the meeting at 6:19pm.
Bill West Aye
Tara B. White Aye
Beth Dean Aye

TOWN OF EGREMONT, MASSACHUSETTS
MEETING OF THE SELECT BOARD
MINUTES
******************************************************************************
Date: March 31, 2026
Time: 10:00 A.M.
Place: Via Zoom Meeting & Town Hall
Egremont
Present at the meeting in person were Select Board Chairwoman Lucinda Vermeulen, Vice
Chairwoman Laura Allen, Board Member Mary Brazie, Administrative Assistant Mindy Nilson,
Emily Eyre, Mindi Morin, Judith Goodman, Web Administrator Mary McGurn, Leslie Alfin,
Amanda Curnin, Town Clerk/Board of Health Director Juliette Haas, Police Chief Jason
LaForest, and Ashley Zabian.
Present via zoom were Marj Wexler, Charles Ogden, Dan Blitzer and Personnel Director Cara
Becker.
The meeting was audio and video recorded.
ACCEPTANCE OF MINUTES:
The minutes of March 17 and March 24 meetings were accepted as presented.
SCHEDULED ISSUES:
Police Chief Jason LaForest appeared before the Select Board to introduce Ashley Zabian
as a prospective candidate for the Police Academy and a potential future police officer.
Ashley will first undergo a physical examination with her physician to determine if she is
medically qualified to apply to the academy. If she meets the requirements, she will then
complete the Physical Ability Test (PAT). Upon successful completion of these steps, the
department will proceed with identifying an academy with available openings and work to enroll
her in the earliest session possible.
NEW BUSINESS:
Mindi Morin of The Prospect appeared before the Select Board to request a one-day
extension of hours for their liquor license. The current license permits alcohol service until 11:00
PM. Due to a wedding scheduled at The Prospect on June 6, 2026, they requested approval to
extend alcohol service until 1:00 AM for that day only.
Additionally, they requested permission to use French Park as a parking area for the
wedding party on June 5, 2026, from 5:00 PM to 11:00 PM.
The Select Board approved both requests for one day only.
The Select Board unanimously appointed Emily Eyre to the French Park Dog Park
Committee.
Emily Eyre presented a proposal to the Select Board to install a sally port gate system at
the French Park Dog Park to help prevent small dogs from escaping. After obtaining three quotes
from nearby businesses, All-American Fence was selected as the contractor, with a total project
cost of $2,880.
The Select Board confirmed approval for Emily to raise funds for the gate. Donations
made to the Town of Egremont for the French Park Dog Park will be tax-deductible.
Town Clerk Juliette Haas presented two candidates she recommended as fill-in poll
workers. Amanda Curnin and Leslie Alfin were unanimously appointed by the Select Board to
fill these positions.
OLD BUSINESS:
Mary McGurn spoke with the Select Board regarding compliance with the Department of
Justice accessibility requirements for municipal websites, deciding to postpone any action until
after consulting with the Berkshire Regional Planning Commission.
Board of Health Director Juliette Haas spoke to the Select Board about the Berkshire
Health Alliance contract. The Board reviewed a proposed increase from $13,000 to $24,000 to
include 30 days of training for a new health agent, with discussion about potentially structuring
the training as a separate per diem contract to avoid unnecessary overlap in payments. More
research will be done and will be brought before the Select Board at a later date.
GRANTS:
Grant Administrator Peg McDonough was not present at the meeting; therefore, the grant
portion of the agenda was tabled until the next scheduled meeting.
SELECT BOARD ITEMS:
Next meeting:
April 7, 2026 10am budget meeting/town meeting
April 14, 2026 regular meeting
Adjournment 10:56 am
Mindy Nilson
Administrative Assistant

The Board discussed areas where it can reduce the FY 27 budget, primarily by not fully funding

additional contingency hours but not the requested wage increase. The FY 27 budget includes
the 3% COLA.

retired. The Highway Department has hired an on call employee for winter storms which will be

Date: April 7, 2026

Egremont
Present at the meeting in person were Select Board Chairwoman Lucinda Vermeulen, Vice-Chairwoman
Laura Allen, Board member Mary Brazie, Administrative Assistant Mindy Nilson, Cemetery Chairman
David Campbell, and Judith Goodman.
Present via zoom were Web Administrator Mary McGurn, Grant Admin. Peg McDonough, and Finance
Committee member Dan Blitzer.
The meeting was audio and video recorded.
The Select Board meeting focused on finalizing the budget and warrant for FY27.
OTHER BUSINESS:
The Select Board unanimously appointed the following individuals to be flaggers for road
details, Trevor Hoff, Zach Cochran, Dave Katzenstein, Matt Schiff, Jim Noe, and retired Police Chief
Brian Shaw.
Mary Brazie discussed the zoom meeting that the town administrators from five towns held, to
discuss the school budget situation. Due to significant financial discrepancies discovered in the school's
books dating back several years, the group decided to request that the school committee defer budget
certification until later in the season, with towns holding special meetings in June to address the school
budget. The Select Board will sign and send a letter to the school committee requesting deferral of the
school budget submission and coordinate with other towns for unified approach.
Town Administrator Mary Brazie will finalize the warrant and send to Select Board for review
by April 14th. Mary will also redraft the borrowing articles’ wording to ensure they are proper borrowing
articles for the warrant.
Mary will follow up with Harold Scheid for the override amount needed for the May ballot and
update the ballot question wording as necessary.
BUDGET ITEMS:
The cemetery commission requested two budget amendments: increasing cemetery maintenance
expenses from $36,800 to $40,000 due to expected gas price increases, and raising cemetery projects
funding from $10,000 to $12,000. The Select Board approved additional funding request.
The Select Board reduced the landfill PFAS monitoring special article budget from $17,000 to
$12,500 due to successful well drilling.
The Select Board approved funding for Berkshire Health Alliance services in the amount of
$21,500. Additionally, $2,500 was approved for the Inspector of Animals, along with $500 set aside to
cover any rabies-related issues that may arise.
The Select Board reviewed the warrant articles for the upcoming town meeting, including a
proposed tax override for the school budget and debt exclusions for vehicle purchases.
Dan Blitzer with the Finance Committee raised concerns about potential tax increases from
special articles, though specific numbers were not finalized.

Housing Trust Board - Jointly with the Planning Board
Information Session, April 8, 2026, 5:30pm
Present at Town Hall were: Mary Brazie, Doug Mishkin, Donna Bersch-Gordon, John Lanterman, Ed
Regendhal, Evan Hardcastle, Judi Goodman, Laura Allen, Bruce Mallory, Steve Cohen, Rebecca
Heidgerd, Elliott Snyder, Cathy Clark, Steve Goodman, Richard Allen, Bruce & Sandi Kaufenbaum,
Erica Randlett, Heather Thomson, Al Thorp, Juliette Haas, Joan Goodkind, Dan Blitzer
Present Via Zoom: Mary McGurn, Blake McDonald, Lauren Shultz, Elys Shuster, Jody Burrows, Liz
Wilson, Ron Banks, Kathy O’Malley, Rebecca Turner, Karen Watkins, Nic, Fred Gordon, Ellen Rudley,
Maureen Cohen, Neil DeLuca, Lavine, Richard Stanley, Lynne Sebatian, George Klemp, Darya Geeter,
Charles Pelton, Lucinda Vermeulen, Sam Handel, MJ Marx, Bryan Frank, Unkowns: IPad 8, 202-494-
5694
The meeting was an information session focused on discussing proposed zoning and general bylaws
regarding short-term rentals (STRs) in Egremont.
The Planning Board and Housing Trust presented their draft regulations, which would permit STRs by
right in certain districts while implementing specific site-based standards like parking requirements.
Mary McGurn, Chair of Planning Board, presented a draft zoning bylaw aimed at providing clarity on
short-term rentals, which currently has no explicit regulation in the town's bylaws. The draft defines
short-term rentals as those lasting 31 days or less and permits them by right in both village districts and
rural residential districts. It introduces three site-based considerations: parking (based on the number of
bedrooms plus one), access, and lighting standards. The board clarified that these requirements only apply
to licensed short-term rentals and do not affect regular single-family homes, as they are specifically
designed to address site impacts of short-term rental operations.
Kathy O'Malley expressed concerns about high registration fees for short-term rentals, noting that rental
tax revenue goes to the town. Elliot Snyder and Bruce Mallory raised questions about parking limitations,
with Elliot questioning the rationale behind the 90-day limit and Bruce asking about options for additional
cars during special events at resideces.
Charles Pelon raised concerns about the bureaucratic process for occasional rentals, while Bryan Frank
highlighted issues with limiting short-term rentals to accessory use only and suggested improvements to
the general bylaw. Mary clarified that under the state definition, short-term rentals are properties rented
for 31 days or less, with an exemption for rentals of 14 days or less throughout the year.
Doug Mishkin, Vice-Chair of the Housing Trust, presented the Trust's proposed general bylaw regarding
short-term rentals. He explained that while the current zoning does not allow short-term rentals and the
proposed Zoning Bylaw will allow STR’s, the Housing Trust believes they should be regulated as
businesses to address the town's housing crisis. The proposed bylaw distinguishes between existing
residents using their homes for short-term rentals and new property buyers using rentals primarily for
profit, aiming to discourage the latter. The bylaw defines short-term rentals as properties rented for 31
consecutive days or less, with rentals of 32 or more days exempt from the regulations. Current owners
with registered properties can continue operating indefinitely, while future owners will be subject to new
restrictions. The bylaw introduces a $400 initial registration fee and $300 annual renewal fee, along with
a cap of 50 short-term rental properties in Egremont. For the first two years after implementation, existing
registered owners can operate without night limits, but after that period, a maximum of 90 nights per year
will be allowed for all owners, with the goal of discouraging property purchases for primary investment
purposes while allowing residents to maintain necessary income.
Several current short-term rental owners expressed concerns about the one-size-fits-all approach,
particularly regarding the 90-day limit, noting that their expenses and needs vary significantly. The
Housing Trust emphasized that these regulations are intended to address housing affordability issues and
deter short-term rentals from becoming primarily business activities.
Blake McDonald and his wife Lauren, who operate a short-term rental at 93 Undermountain, expressed
concerns about the proposed 90-night cap, arguing it would make their business un-viable and force them
to sell their property. They suggested a compromise of 150 nights, aligning with Great Barrington's
regulations, and emphasized that their rental serves families seeking affordable vacation options different
from those offered by local B&Bs. Joan Goodkind also spoke in support of short-term rentals, noting that
many residents depend on this income to afford living in the town due to rising costs and taxes.
Several residents, including Kathy O'Malley and Darya Geeter, expressed concerns about proposed
bylaws that would restrict STRs to 90 days per year and require $400 annual registration fees. Residents
like Doug Neil and Rebecca Heidgerd raised objections, noting that these restrictions could deter future
investments in the community and fail to address affordable housing needs. The discussion highlighted
tensions between regulating STRs and supporting local economic development, with some residents
arguing that the proposed limits were overly restrictive and poorly understood by the board.
Fred Gordon and Neil DeLuca expressed strong opposition to the proposed 50-unit cap and 90-day limit,
arguing that these restrictions would be overly restrictive and harmful to property owners who rely on
STR income. They suggested implementing a floating cap based on a percentage of total housing stock
(around 10%) and increasing the maximum rental period to at least 120 days. Heather Thompson, who
owns a local business and property, advocated for a balanced approach that would allow some STRs
while addressing affordable housing needs.
The Planning Board hearing regarding the proposed zoning bylaw is being held on April 14.
The Planning Board and Housing Trust will hold another community session on April 29th.
The Special Town Meeting at which these proposals will be discussed is scheduled for June 10.
Mary Brazie,
Recording Secretary

--- MINUTES ---

TRANSFER STATION WORKING GROUP MEETING
April 9, 2026 – Approved May 28, 2026
The meeting was called to order at approximately 3:30 PM by Freddy Friedman with Tara
White, Marc Trachtenberg, Chuck Loring (partial), and Gardiner Morse in attendance.
Agenda
1) Review and approve minutes; 2) Mission statements; 3) Attendant job descriptions; 4)
Communications; 5) Permit process; 6) Other business.
Approval of Minutes
The minutes of the 3-20-26 meeting were approved with minor changes.
Mission Statements
The meeting opened with a discussion of draft mission statements for both the Transfer Station
and the Working Group.
Marc introduced revised language developed from regional models and state guidance, noting
that while the Working Group has an existing mission statement, the Transfer Station itself
does not currently have a clear, public-facing mission statement. The proposed draft focuses on
safe, efficient, and cost-effective waste disposal, regulatory compliance, and increased recycling
and reuse.
Discussion quickly turned to how best to balance clarity with completeness. Members generally
agreed that the mission statement itself should be short and accessible, with more detailed
responsibilities and priorities captured separately in a supporting mandate.
From there, the conversation broadened into two larger themes. The first was the question
of financial sustainability, including whether and how the station might move over time to
break-even or profitability. The second was the Town’s potential financial exposure associated
with the leased transfer station site, particularly the obligation to remediate the property if the
lease were not renewed. While not a new issue, Marc emphasized that there is no record of
this exposure or its magnitude and it has not been formally accounted for. Freddy will consult
with Mari regarding how this liability is currently treated and whether additional analysis is
required.
The group agreed to review the draft mission and mandate documents individually and return
to the topic at a future meeting. There was also agreement to seek clarification from Town
Counsel on Open Meeting Law questions raised during the discussion, including whether a staff
or third-party resource could be used to support communication among members outside
formal meetings without violating the Open Meeting Law.
Attendant Job Descriptions
The group then turned to a review of Gardiner’s draft job descriptions for transfer station
attendants. The draft reflects a shift toward a more structured staffing model, with all
attendants able to perform core operational tasks and a senior attendant assuming additional
responsibility for oversight, coordination, and reporting.
Discussion focused on making sure the job descriptions reflect the realities of the work without
being unnecessarily restrictive. Members discussed training and safety requirements, physical
demands (eg the ability to lift 50 pounds), and how responsibilities such as fee collection and
equipment operation should be handled.
There was general agreement that formal educational requirements (such as a high school
diploma or GED) should be removed to avoid narrowing the applicant pool, and that the
description of hours should allow for flexibility rather than specifying a fixed schedule.
Overall, the draft was seen as a strong starting point that will benefit from further refinement.
Gardiner will revise the job descriptions based on feedback and circulate an updated draft.
Communications
Gardiner then presented a draft assessment of current station communications and a proposal
for improvement.
The discussion highlighted a persistent challenge: the station communicates through at least six
channels—the town website, email alerts, Maggie’s List, the Five Village News, Instagram, and
on-site signage—but those channels are not always well coordinated and the information
disseminated on them can be inconsistent, contradictory, out of date, inaccurate or reach only
a limited portion of residents.
Members agreed that improving communications could have practical benefits across several
areas, including compliance with station rules, participation in recycling programs, and
awareness of closures or schedule changes and enhancing resident understanding of station
operations. The relatively low level of participation in the town’s alert system (just 81 of the
town’s roughly 400 permit holders subscribe) was noted in particular as needing improvement.
Possible next steps discussed included increasing alert enrollment (potentially through an opt-
out approach at permit issuance) and exploring ways to ensure that accurate, timely
information is distributed consistently across channels.
The conversation also touched briefly on the idea of developing a clearer visual identity for the
station—a logo or branding that could help make communications more visible and engaging—
while keeping any such effort appropriately scaled and grounded in the station’s day-to-day
needs. Gardiner presented a mock-up of a proposed station patch, suggesting that it could be
used on station gear or other items made available to the public to build pride in and support
for the station.
Permit Process
The group then discussed a proposed revision to the permit process present by Tara, based on
a model used in Sheffield. Under that approach, all households would receive an annual mailing
requiring them to indicate whether they use the transfer station or a private waste service, with
the goal of ensuring that all households are accounted for in one system or the other.
Members noted that such a system could improve both compliance and visibility into how
waste is handled across the town. Tara emphasized the administrative work involved, including
collecting accurate addresses, possibility of requiring waste haulers to report service addresses,
managing mailings and confirmation of permit purchases and the need for a volunteer to take
on this work rather than asking Town Hall staff to absorb further Transfer Station work. Marc
agreed to pursue the initial steps involved in collecting current resident mailing addresses.
The concept was received with interest, with agreement that further work is needed to assess
how it might be implemented in New Marlborough.
Other Business
Tara raised the issue of prioritizing the Working Group’s expanding list of action items. Marc
noted that the Station redesign and implementation of the point-of-purchase system should
remain top priorities. Gardiner pointed out that the existing “Action Items” spreadsheet on the
Group’s shared Google Drive could facilitate the prioritization process. The group agreed to
return to the prioritization question at the next meeting.
Adjournment
With no further business, the meeting adjourned at 5:20 PM
Submitted by: Gardiner Morse

Housing Trust Board
Meeting April 10, 2026, 8:00am
Present at Town Hall were Housing Trust Board members Mary Brazie, Evan Hardcastel, and Judith
Goodman, as well as Mary McGurn, MJ Marx, and Bruce Mallory.
Present via zoom were Housing Trust Board Chairman Richard Stanley, Vice-Chairman Doug
Mishkin, Lucinda Vermeulen, Lori Hains and Blake McDonald.
The meeting was audio and video recorded.
Community Preservation Act Funding Allocation
The Board will discuss in detail at its next meeting the possibility of the Community Preservation
Committee awarding funds to the Trust for future housing projects.
Zoning Board of Appeals 40B Hearing
It was noted that the Zoning Board of Appeals hearing on the CDC’s Chapter 40B application for the
town’s housing project takes place at 5pm today. Richard explained the format of 40B hearings,
where the ZBA is the commanding body and other boards are invited to participate. Richard
highlighted that 40B hearings are unique in allowing developers to receive permits with only health
or safety caveats, and cannot impose economic burdens on projects.
Short-Term Rental Regulation
The Board discussed amendments to the short-term rentals general bylaw based on feedback at the
information session earlier in the week. It was emphasized that a 150-day cap was what current
owners of Short-tern rental could be happy with. The Board agreed to an exception for owner-
occupied premises, allowing unlimited nights for those who rent rooms within their homes. The
question of owner-occupied properties with rental apartments and ADU’s was not determined. The
Board also discussed potentially lowering the proposed cap on STRs to a % of approximately 10%.
The next meeting was scheduled for April 16th at 8 AM.
It was noted that the public hearing on the zoning by-law is set for April 14th and a second
information meeting is scheduled for April 29.
Meeting adjourned at 9:01am.

EGREMONT GREEN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES
Tuesday, April 14, 2026, at 3:00 PM, at Town Hall and via Zoom
Welcome and Introduction of guests: Chair Emily Eyre opened the meeting at 3:00 PM and
welcomed everyone. Those attending in person: Emily Eyre, Juliette Haas, and Marj Wexler,
and guest Stephanie Blumenthal. Attending via Zoom: Bonnie Greenwood, Sharon Waskow and
Associate Member Sue Fine.
Meeting Minutes: Motion made and seconded to approve the meeting minutes of 3/17/26.
Approved by unanimous vote. Schedule of taking minutes: Bonnie in May, and Juliette in June.
Sustainability Report: Juliette reported that she will make an application for a Green
Communities grant issued by DEP by the end of the week. A grant is expected for our recycling,
reuse initiatives. This includes remuneration for the Earth Day road cleanup pizza party costs.
The grant is for $1500 and we find out in November.
New Business: According to the Springfield MRF, paper and plastic cups are now recyclable.
Paper goes in paper recycling and clear plastic cups such as the kind ice coffee comes in, go to
the plastic recycling bin. Marj has posted this information on NeighborNet. Bonnie asked if the
paper cups are recyclable even with their plastic liners. Juliette responded that a process
separates the lining from the cup. Waste Management, the company that operates the
Springfield MRF, specifies that only the cups, not straws or lids, are recyclable.
The committee discussed creating educational materials, including postcards and posters, using
RDP funds for implementation. No immediate decision was made on timing.
Stephanie Blumenthal updated the group on the upcoming food waste film screening of “Just
Eat It” at the Triplex on June 3. She mentioned partnering with the group Refed and the
potential of working with farmers on sending the food left over in fields to the Food Pantry. This
is called gleaning. The following food shops were approached about supplying food at the
event: the Bagel company, Guido’s, Patisserie. She also mentioned that the culinary division at
Mt. Everett School uses recipes for leftovers. She posed the idea of asking kids to prepare
something for the event from leftovers. Posters are needed to educate and promote the event.
It was suggested that a poster could mention the methane created when food is thrown in trash.
Bonnie suggested promoting compost bins which Egremont currently sells to residents for $25.
The committee agreed to explore expanding this program to Sheffield.
Upcoming events. The group discussed the upcoming pizza dinner after the road cleanup and
what food would be provided. So far 18, attendees have RSVP’d. Attendees will be asked to
bring their own cutlery and plates. An October event with ProShred was tentatively scheduled
for Oct 10 from 1-3 to align with the Transfer Station’s closing time. Funding for the shredding
part of the event will be pursued with NBT (formerly Salisbury Bank.) The event will also involve
the Freon-removal company, IRRI (Interstate Refrigerant Recovery, Inc)., and the committee will
offer invitations to Sheffield. Traffic management at the event was also discussed and will be
revisited as we get closer to the event.
Microplastics Survey. The Berkshire Regional Planning Commission has offered to create a
survey about community preferences for plastic reduction measures. The survey will consist of
5-10 questions to determine residents’ interests and preferences. Committee members were
asked to write 2-3 questions and submit them to Juliette by April 28. Sharon informed the group
of the upcoming screening of the documentary “The Plastic Detox” at Mason Library in Great
Barrington on April 16 from 1-3. It’s available to download from Netflix.
The committee noted the passing of associate member Jane Marcus, and made plans to send
condolences and share her obituary.
The next Green Committee meeting is scheduled for May 19 at 4:30 PM, with Wednesday the
20th as the backup.
The meeting was adjourned at 4:03 PM.
Respectfully submitted,
Sharon Waskow

Egremont Planning Board Draft Minutes
Public Hearing on Short-term Rental Zoning Amendments
• Meeting date: April 14, 2026
• Location: In person at Egremont Town Hall and via Zoom
• Chair: Mary McGurn
• Board members present: John Lanterman, Stephen Lyle, Donna Bersch-Gordon, Eddie
Regendahl.
• Guests: Judi Goodman, Blake McDonald, Liz Wilson, Marj Wexler, Neal Goff, Darya
Geether, Bruce Mallory, Steve Cohen, Joan Goodkind,
• Call to Order time: 5:30 PM
• Adjournment time: 6:33 PM
• Next meeting date/time: TBD
Other scheduled meetings mentioned in the hearing included a Municipal Housing Trust
meeting on Thursday, April 16, 2026 at 8:00 AM; an additional short-term-rental
informational/listening session on April 29, 2026 and a Special Town Meeting on June 10, 2026
Key Outputs
• Chair Mary McGurn opened the public hearing on the proposed short-term rental zoning
bylaw amendment and clarified that the hearing addressed only the zoning article, not
the separate general bylaw being drafted by the Municipal Housing Trust.
• The Board explained that the zoning amendment is intended to end the bylaw’s current
silence on short-term rentals by defining the use, allowing it by right in all districts, and
establishing site-based standards for off-street parking, vehicular circulation/access, and
exterior lighting.
• Public comment focused primarily on the proposed parking standard and how it would
apply to owner-occupied homes, single-room rentals, performers or artists housed
without cash payment, and other operating scenarios.
• Board members stated they are considering adding a parking waiver provision so the
Planning Board may waive strict parking compliance when full compliance is not
reasonably feasible, on-site parking remains sufficient for expected demand, and no
adverse impacts are created.
• Motion/Vote: Motion by John Lanterman to close the public hearing on the proposed
short-term rental zoning bylaw; second by Donna Bersch-Gordon; roll-call vote yes by
Donna Bersch-Gordon, Stephen Lye, John Lanterman, Eddie Regendahl, and Mary
McGurn; outcome: motion carried unanimously and the hearing was closed.
Discussion
Opening and hearing scope
Chair Mary McGurn called the hearing to order at 5:30 PM on Tuesday, April 14, 2026. She
identified Planning Board members participating in person and by Zoom and identified
attendees in the room and online.
McGurn stated that the hearing was a duly noticed public hearing on the proposed zoning bylaw
amendment regarding short-term rentals. She emphasized that the hearing concerned only the
zoning bylaw article and not the separate general bylaw under development by the Municipal
Housing Trust.
McGurn also noted that both the zoning bylaw and the general bylaw were expected to go
before a Special Town Meeting on June 10, 2026.
Why the zoning amendment is being proposed
McGurn explained that under Massachusetts zoning practice, if a use is not defined and
permitted in the zoning bylaw, it is not allowed. She stated that because Egremont’s zoning
bylaw is currently silent on short-term rentals, the amendment is intended to correct that
silence and provide certainty for operators, neighbors, and the Town.
Board members and participants discussed the distinction between the two proposed bylaws.
The zoning bylaw would define short-term rentals as a land use, establish where the use is
allowed, and set site-related standards. The general bylaw would address operating rules such
as registration, fees, complaints, and enforcement.
Proposed short-term rental definition
McGurn presented the proposed definition of a short-term rental as the use of a dwelling unit,
residential structure, or a portion of one for 31 consecutive days or fewer in exchange for
payment. She stated that the language mirrors the state definition used for room occupancy tax
purposes and excludes hotels, inns, and bed-and-breakfasts, which are addressed elsewhere in
zoning.
Darya Geether questioned how the definition would apply to consecutive stays by different
guests and to non-cash compensation such as tickets provided to a host housing performers.
Blake McDonald responded that separate stays of fewer than 31 days would still be separate
short-term rentals. McGurn stated that the discussion suggested barter-type arrangements may
fall outside the cash-payment concept, and Judi Goodman stated that the question should be
brought to Town Counsel.
The Board noted concern that the treatment of performers, artists, and similar temporary
guests may need additional clarification. No specific change to the definition was directed at
this hearing.
Where the use would be allowed
McGurn stated that the zoning proposal would allow short-term rentals by right in all districts,
including the North Egremont village district, South Egremont village district, and rural
residential district.
No formal change to the proposed district approach was made during the hearing.
Site-based standards and relation to noise bylaw
McGurn explained that the zoning proposal includes three site-based conditions: off-street
parking, vehicular circulation and access, and exterior lighting. She stated that these standards
were intended to address external impacts on abutters and the Town.
McGurn also stated that noise was not included in the zoning proposal because the Town had
already adopted a separate noise bylaw in October 2025 and that bylaw had since been
approved by the Attorney General with a minor change. She described noise as an operational
or behavioral issue handled through the general bylaw framework rather than zoning.
Parking discussion and potential waiver
McGurn summarized the proposed off-street parking standard as one parking space per
bedroom plus one additional space, all located on the lot and arranged to reduce headlight
glare onto neighboring properties.
Joan Goodkind raised concern about whether the bylaws would address the purchase of a
house solely for short-term rental use. McGurn and Judi Goodman responded that ownership,
occupancy status, and related operating limits would be addressed through the general bylaw
rather than the zoning bylaw.
Bruce Mallory raised detailed questions about how the parking requirement would apply to an
owner-occupied home renting only one bedroom, including whether the short-term rental
parking would be added to the minimum parking already associated with the principal dwelling.
McGurn stated that an owner-occupied house with a short-term rental would involve two uses
under one roof—a principal dwelling and a short-term rental—and that the parking
requirements for both uses would apply. Board members acknowledged that the issue was
complex and warranted further clarification.
Darya Geether also stated that a rigid parking formula could negatively affect residents who
host performers or artists who may not arrive with vehicles, and she urged the Town to consider
how those situations would be handled.
McGurn presented draft waiver language under discussion by the Planning Board that would
allow the Board to waive strict parking compliance when lot conditions make full compliance
not reasonably feasible, on-site parking remains sufficient for expected demand, and the
reduced arrangement would not create adverse impacts on traffic safety, driveway or
emergency access, or neighboring properties.
Mallory questioned how a waiver would be enforced if the approved number of short-term-
rental-related vehicles were exceeded. Board members and participants discussed possible
enforcement through the building inspector, police ticketing for overnight street parking, and
the general bylaw’s licensing framework. No final enforcement mechanism was considered by
the Planning Board at this hearing.
Board members John Lanterman, Donna Bersch-Gordon, and Eddie Regendahl each stated that
the comments were useful, that short-term rental situations vary substantially, and that a
waiver process could provide needed flexibility and balance.

The Select Board postponed discussion regarding the Council on Aging holiday dinner.
Grant Administrator Peg McDonough addressed the Select Board regarding the Town’s
recent Green Communities grant award. The funding will support improvements to the insulation
at the water treatment plant, with the goal of reducing propane usage and lowering energy costs.
The Select Board also approved a press release drafted by Peg announcing the award.
The Select Board approved an application for entertainment and a one day only beer/wine
license for Blue Rider Stables to host a summer benefit on June 6, 2026.
OLD BUSINESS:
The demolition delay bylaw has been tabled.
GRANTS:
Grant Administrator Peg McDonough provided updates on several grant initiatives,
including the One Stop Rural Development Fund supporting dam rehabilitation work, as well as
a pending MassDOT culvert replacement grant. She also reviewed the status of the Karner Brook
dam alternatives study, which is expected to be completed by the end of May, and will present
the proposed alternatives along with associated costs to the board.
BUDGET:
The Select Board discussed the town warrant and school budget issues. They decided to
leave the school budget line item blank on the warrant as to not confuse people. Lucinda also
noted that Dr. Ricka and Julie Hannum would attend the upcoming town meeting to explain the
budget situation. The warrant will be signed and posted by the constable no later than Friday
April 17, 2026.

CPA funding:
The committee briefly discussed two models for allocating funds:
allowing individual applications or giving designated entities (like
the housing trust) direct allocation authority. Richard strongly
favored the second model, arguing it would allow faster response to
housing opportunities. More detailed discussion will take place a
future meeting.
CDC Housing Project:
It was noted that there have been over 40 expressions of interest for
housing. The Zoning Board Appeals has unanimously approved the
Chapter 40B Comprehensive Permit.
Short-term rentals:
It was agreed to exempt individual room rentals in owner-occupied
dwellings from short-term rental regulations. The planning board's
parking requirements would continue to apply to these situations.
Voted by a majority vote to cap the number of properties at 50, with
Evan being the only dissenting vote. On the number of nights per
year, it was unanimous to establish a cap of 150 nights. Agreed to
drop two waiting periods from their short-term rental bylaw: the
one-year waiting period after a long-term lease expires, and the 6-
month waiting period after property acquisition. Doug and Judi will
edit the draft bylaw.
Richard mentioned a potential update on a revolving loan fund for
affordable housing after meeting with John Bissell from Greylock
Savings Bank which he report on at a future meeting.
The next meeting was scheduled for Tuesday, April 28th at 8 AM, with
a public information session on short-term rentals and seasonal
communities designations scheduled for April 29th.

Select Board
Monday, April 27, 2026
6pm
Board Members Present: Tara White

Beth Dean

David Hastings, American Legion Post 350
Ann Riou, American Legion Post 350
Beth Dean called the meeting to order at 6:00pm.
Pledge of Allegiance and Moment of Silence for Veterans
The Pledge of Allegiance was recited and a moment of silence for Veterans was held.
Discuss upcoming Memorial Day Observance
Dave Hastings said the usual Memorial Day parade and observance will take place on May 25th.
He said it will be relatively the same as previous years. Jesse Carpenter, the principal of Mt.
Everett High School, will be the featured speaker. Robert Olsen will be the pastor. Barbara
Marchione is making wreaths for the headstones.
Hear updates and discuss next steps on relocation of Veterans’ Memorials
Dave Hastings said the American Legion Post 350 unanimously voted to not relocate the
monuments to land that has a revocable lease. Therefore, the Legion is not interested in moving
forward with the proposal from the Meetinghouse offering the site on the corner of Route 57 and
New Marlborough Southfield Road as it doesn’t consider that a permanent home. Ann Riou said
they are still open to other reasonable locations in the Village of New Marlborough. Ann also
said she has names to add to the list of veterans to be listed on the monuments.
1
Review and sign contracts: Fire Chief, Highway Superintendent, Town Administrator
Mari Enoch explained that the Fire Chief contract is still for one year and includes a $15,000
stipend. The only change in the contract from the previous year is that Chief is eligible to receive
compensation for responding to fire and ambulance calls outside of his regularly scheduled work
day, at the same rate as other on-call Fire Fighters.
Beth made a motion, Tara seconded, and it was so voted to sign the contract between the
Town and Fire Chief Charles Loring with an annual stipend of $15,000 effective from July
1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.
Bill West Aye
Tara B. White Aye
Beth Dean Aye
Mari said the Highway Superintendent salary increased by about 10% to $110,745 to keep up
with other highway department rate increases and keep a wage differential between the Highway
Foreman and Superintendent.
Beth made a motion, Tara seconded, and it was so voted to sign the contract between the
Town and Highway Superintendent Charles Loring with an annual salary of $110,745
effective from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.
Bill West Aye
Tara B. White Aye
Beth Dean Aye
Beth said there were no changes to the Town Administrator other than the COLA compensation
increase to $67,027 per year.
Beth made a motion, Tara seconded, and so voted to sign the contract between the Town
and Town Administrator Mari Enoch with an annual salary of $67,027 per year effective
July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.
Bill West Aye
Tara B. White Aye
Beth Dean Aye
Review and renew lease with New Marlborough Volunteer Fire Company
Mari said the Fire Department buildings and garages are used to house the Fire/Rescue
Department, Police Department, and Emergency Management. The Town uses the building for
other meetings, including Town Meeting. No changes have been made to the yearly lease.
2
Beth made a motion, Tara seconded, and it was so voted to approve and authorize Beth
Dean to sign the lease agreement between the Town of New Marlborough and the New
Marlborough Volunteer Fire Company for $18,000 per year, from July 1, 2026 through
June 30, 2027.
Bill West Aye
Tara B. White Aye
Beth Dean Aye
Appoint Animal Inspector
Mari explained that the state’s term for Animal Inspector is May 1st to April 30th. Prue
Spaulding is the current Animal Inspector and agreed to continue in the role.
Beth made a motion, Tara seconded, and it was so voted to appoint Prue Spaulding as the
Animal Inspector, effective May 1, 2026 through April 30, 2027.
Bill West Aye
Tara B. White Aye
Beth Dean Aye

Gould Farm sent a letter to the Select Board requesting permission to post signage along
roadways in New Marlborough for their upcoming 5k race on Sunday, May 30.
Beth made a motion, Tara seconded, and it was so voted to allow Gould Farm to place signs
in New Marlborough two weeks before the event. The signs are to be taken down within 48
hours of the event.
Bill West Aye
Tara B. White Aye
Beth Dean Aye

Mari said the Cable Advisory and Broadband Committee is looking for a new Digital Navigator,
and will consider hiring two people to share the position. The Police Dept. Admin position is on
hold at the moment. Printed copies of the Annual Report are available at Town Hall and Library,
and the report is also posted on the website.

The Board agreed to meet on Monday, May 4th at 8:30 am, and at 6pm before Town Meeting at
7 pm. Tara White said she would like to follow up with the status of the Cassilis project at a
future meeting.

Present in person at Town Hall were members Richard Stanley, Doug Mishkin, Mary Brazie,
Judith Goodman and Evan Hardcastle, and John Lanterman. Present via zoom were, Mary
McGurn, and Blake McDonald.
CPA Funding Allocation Discussion
Discussion took place regarding the Community Preservation Act (CPA) funding and the Housing
Trust's potential allocation of these funds. Doug outlined four possible categories for potential CPA
funding use, including property acquisition, site preparation for additional units, down payment
assistance, and purchasing deed restrictions from property owners converting to short-term rentals.
The group agreed to advocate for the Housing Trust to receive 80% of the CPA funds allocated to
housing as a bucket allotment, arguing that this would allow more timely and efficient use of funds
without requiring annual town meeting approval for specific projects. The first CPA funding process
will begin in fall 2026, with town meeting approval expected in May 2027.
Short-Term Rental Bylaw Revisions
The Board discussed revisions to the short-term rental bylaw, focusing on adjusting the cap on rental
nights to 150 and exempting room rentals within a full house from this cap. They agreed to remove
waiting periods for converting long-term rentals to short-term rentals and for new short-term rental
owners.
The group scheduled a follow-up meeting for Friday at 1 PM to finalize the revised bylaw language,
which needs to be delivered to the Select Board by May 5th for the June 10th town meeting warrant.
The Board also briefly discussed the upcoming information session and presentation on seasonal
communities designation, with Mary McGurn and Doug planning to co-present on this topic.

Housing Trust Board
Informational Meeting
April 29, 2026 - 5:30pm
Short-Term Rental Zoning Bylaw
Mary McGurn, chair of the planning board, presented an updated version of the short-term rental
zoning bylaw at an informational session. She explained that current zoning lacks definitions for
short-term rentals, making all existing ones illegal, and outlined the proposed bylaw's key
elements: defining short-term rentals, setting site-based standards, and allowing them by right in
all districts. The bylaw includes off-street parking requirements with a waiver option, vehicle
circulation and access standards, and exterior lighting regulations. Mary noted that operational
rules, registration, licensing, and enforcement would be addressed in a separate general bylaw
presented by Doug Mishkin's team.
Mary clarified that short-term rentals lasting 31 days or less require specific off-street parking
based on the number of bedrooms, plus one additional space, while long-term rentals (32+ days)
follow existing parking requirements for the property type. Several participants expressed
concerns about the parking requirements being overly restrictive, particularly for families and
private residents, though Mary explained these were implemented to address potential
commercial impacts. The discussion included information about a waiver process available to
property owners who cannot meet the parking requirements. Othes expressed concerns about the
undefined nature of parking spots and the potential impact on property owners. The Planning
Board will be meeting Friday at 9 AM to evaluate comments and make decisions on the draft
bylaw, with a deadline to submit the draft by May 5th and publish the warrant by May 22nd for a
possible special town meeting on June 10th.
Short-Term Rental General Bylaw Regulations
Doug Mishkin for the Housing Trust presented significant changes to the proposed STR bylaw,
including increasing the annual night cap from 90 to 150 nights, with the cap not taking effect for
two years after the bylaw implementation. They also introduced a new category for "inactive"
short-term rentals that allows property owners to reserve the right to rent in the future without
current usage or fees. The Board also eliminated waiting periods for property transitions between
long-term and short-term rentals, while maintaining a cap of 50 total STR properties in Egremont
to prevent new registrations once the limit is reached.
Participants debated a proposed cap of 50 short-term rentals. Concerns about the lack of
empirical data supporting claims that reducing short-term rentals would increase long-term
rentals were expressed, while questioning the justification for the 50 cap number. The discussion
also addressed issues around property inheritance and licensing, with clarification that short-term
rental licenses are non-transferable and currently allow non-resident ownership. While some
participants supported a floating cap as a guardrail, concerns were raised about the potential
impact on property owners' rights and the community's demographic composition.
Questions were raised about the reasoning behind specific numerical caps, particularly the
difference between 150 and 365 nights, suggestions were made regarding improvements to
clarify language around short-term rental of entire dwellings versus rooms, and questioning the
requirement to post dog-related information for properties that don't allow pets. There was an
inquiry about registering properties in nominee trusts, with clarification provided that trusts can
register properties but should do so before the regulations take effect. The discussion also
touched on concerns about property ownership entities like trusts and LLCs, with suggestions to
address various legal structures while protecting major assets during life events like divorce.
It was explained that evidence shows short-term rentals have decreased long-term rentals, though
specific data on this relationship is limited. Some participants questioned the $400 fee compared
to neighboring towns' lower fees.
The Board emphasized the need to distinguish between residents renting out their primary homes
temporarily and corporations buying properties solely for short-term rental purposes, arguing that
resident-owned properties should be exempt from strict regulations.
Seasonal Community Desination
The seasonal community designation, is a state program that would provide Egremont with
approximately $80,000 in funding annually if approved at the May 5th town meeting. The
designation would allow the town to implement housing preferences for essential workers and
artists, though it would require some zoning changes including restrictions on tiny homes and
undersized lots. The Housing Trust expressed enthusiastic support for the designation.
Meeting adjourned at 8:01pm.
Mary Brazie,
Recording Secretary

TOWN OF EGREMONT, MASSACHUSETTS
MEETING OF THE SELECT BOARD
MINUTES
******************************************************************************
Date: May 5, 2026
Time: 10:00 A.M.
Place: Via Zoom Meeting & Town Hall
Egremont
Present at the meeting in person were Select Board Chairwoman Lucinda Vermeulen, Vice
Chairwoman Laura Allen, Board Member Mary Brazie, Administrative Assistant Mindy Nilson,
Moderator Steven Cohen, Judi Goodman, Corine Heyes, and Town Clerk/Board of Health
Director Juliette Haas.
Present via zoom were Mary McGurn, Grant Administrator Peg McDonough, Egremont Land
Trust member, Molly Cliff, Elia Del Molino with Greenagers and Personnel Director Cara
Becker.
The meeting was audio and video recorded.
ACCEPTANCE OF MINUTES:
The minutes of April 14, and April 21, 2026 meetings were accepted as presented.
NEW BUSINESS:
Molly Cliff with the Egremont Land Trust along with Elia Del Molino from Greenagers
discussed a proposed pilot project led by Greenagers to manually remove invasive Burning Bush
plants from French Park using hand tools and approximately 20 volunteers, including students
from Waldorf School. The project is scheduled for May 13th from 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM, with
Greenagers handling all insurance and liability coverage. The board approved the project, with
additional discussion about coordinating with Native Habitat Restoration's chemical treatment in
the same area and ensuring proper insurance coverage indemnifying the town.
The Select Board approved a Green Committee collection event to be held at the Town
Hall parking lot on Saturday, October 10th from 1 to 3 PM.
The Select Board discussed a potential collaboration with Casella to establish drop-off
locations in Pittsfield for recyclables bound for the Springfield MRF, though no formal motion
was required as this remains under investigation.
Mary Brazie proposed canceling the June 10th Special Town Meeting to review the
School budget and suggested rescheduling it for either June 24 or June 25, pending school
district feedback on available dates. When Mary receives word from the school she will update.
Grant Administrator Peg McDonough spoke to the Select Board, clarifying that she did
not resign from her position with the Town of Egremont but was informed that her employment
would be terminated and offered a contract with reduced compensation. The Select Board
explained that the change was intended to save on payroll costs and not terminate her
employment, but Peg declined the new contract terms. Despite discussions about potential
benefits and the town's recognition of Peg's contributions, she confirmed her decision to end her
employment, and the board formally accepted her wishes to do so with 2 Select Board members
voting aye and 1 vote abstaining, effective June 30th.
OLD BUSINESS:
The Select Board discussed the Council on Aging holiday dinner. Legal counsel
confirmed that the maximum allowable expenditure is $25 per person. This limitation may affect
both the choice of venue and the feasibility of continuing the dinners altogether. The information
will be shared with the Council on Aging, who will decide how to proceed.
GRANTS:
Grant Administrator Peg McDonough covered several grant applications and funding
updates.
Peg reported on a CSIP grant for Karner Ridge Invasive Management, which will be submitted
for approximately $7,000 with a $7,000 match.
Peg also discussed a MassDOT grant for a Blunt Road culvert upgrade, which received positive
feedback about potential additional funding.
Lastly, Peg reported that the Green Communities Grant has been awarded. This grant will
support the installation of insulation at the Water Department.
BUDGET/TOWN MEETING:
The Select Board focused on planning for an upcoming annual town meeting, with
discussions about the agenda, speakers, and logistics. The group decided on the order of opening
statements, including who would read specific sections and introduce key participants such as the
school superintendent and Finance Committee members. They addressed how to handle the
Finance Committee's recommendations and the process for voting on Proposition 2.5 override
questions. The conversation ended with a note that this was Laura Allen’s last meeting.
Adjournment 11:25 am
Mindy Nilson
Administrative Assistant

--- MINUTES ---

Housing Trust Board
May 12, 2026, 1:01PM
Present in-person were Housing Trust Board members Mary Brazie, Judith Goodman,
Evan Hardcastle and Doug Mishkin, Laura Allen, Joan Goodkind, Mark Phillips and
John Lanterman. Present via zoom were Housing Trust Board Chairman Richard
Stanley, Mary McGurn, Peg McDonough, and Blake McDonald.
The meeting was video and audio recorded.
The meeting focused on discussing a short-term rental general bylaw, specifically
addressing whether future short-term rentals should be limited to Egremont residents. The
group agreed that current short-term rental owners who register their properties before the
effective date should be exempt from residency requirements, but future registrations
would require the owner to be an Egremont resident. They also discussed exempting
certain properties, such as accessory dwelling units (ADUs) and separate rooms in a
resident's home, from the 150-day cap on short-term rentals for Egremont residents.
It was clarified that the 150-day cap would apply to whole-house rentals but not to room
rentals or owner-occupied properties. There was some confusion about the definition of
"owner-occupied," with the group agreeing to use "Egremont resident" instead, though they
noted this distinction might be risky for existing property owners. The discussion confirmed
that current residents who register their properties before the effective date can continue
operating without immediate restrictions, but after two years, all whole-house rentals
would be subject to the 150-night cap.
Mary expressed concerns about the complexity of enforcement and the tight timeline for
finalizing the bylaw before a possible June 16 town meeting, noting the need to submit the
draft to the Select Board by June 1.
The group agreed that using a fixed denominator based on Massachusetts property tax data
would be reliable for establishing the 10% cap.
The group debated the financial aspects of implementing the program, including software
and inspection costs.
Mark Phillips, a resident, emphasized the importance of including Egremont resident
language in the bylaw and expressed support for the proposal contingent on this addition.
The group also discussed concerns about legal entities owning properties for short-term
rentals, with Judy and others noting that LLCs and corporations would still require resident
members to comply with the bylaw.
The group discussed challenges with short-term rentals affecting housing availability and
prices in Egremont.
The Board will meet on May 15 at 7am to review the new draft.
Meeting adjourned at 2:03pm.
Mary Brazie,
Recording Secretary

changes, Warrant #38. PB members provided feedback and discussed tactics in re-presenting bylaw changes at
an upcoming Special Town Meeting tentatively scheduled for the end of June.
 Items that require additional review included
o Alignment of language specific to greenhouses, fur farming and piggeries noted in case law and
Right to Farm.
o Cannabis clarification- separated from the Right to Farm as noted by Town Council not included in
the prior warrant.
o Service and use of municipal and public buildings, currently not included in the warrant.
 Discussion of enhanced education and communication to Town Residents then ensued. Discussion
included the following plans.
o Breaking down the current warrant into several smaller, content specific warrants.
o Identification of key content experts who would present the warrant item and rationale for
requesting the change.
o Post proposed warrants at public locations in advance of the Special Town Meeting so residents
can review. Potentially New Marlborough Library, Town Hall, Southfield Store, Meeting House
Gallery.
o Repost upcoming Public Meeting dates in the Berkshire Eagle, on Maggie’s List and potentially
develop a one-page FAQ sheet/pamphlet which can be distributed in advance.
o Confirm MA state regulations of space required per one breeding sow.
o Consider questions related to slaughterhouses (meat processing facilities) and identify local
expertise to address.
o Discussion regarding the table presented in the existing warrant. Several PB members voiced
concern that this was confusing to voters and recommended including it as an addendum as a
reference item.
 Key content areas for creation of specific warrants, and potential content experts to support.
o Building bylaw changes to comply with July 2025 changes in the MA building codes and clarification
requests from the Building Inspector. Content expert Building Inspector.
o Alignment of agricultural uses to align with Right to Farm and MA case law. Content expert Town
Counsel.
o Cannabis non included in agricultural use bylaw. Content expert Town Counsel.
o Slaughterhouse/meet processing facilities- special permit rural districts only. Content experts Jake
Levin and Tom Braize.
o Use of municipal and public buildings- currently missing in prior warrant Section 3.4.1-10
Action item identify missing language and insert.
 Notification Sequencing
o Building Inspector to review bylaw changes prior to May 26th Planning Board Meeting.
Action Item Jordan Archey to follow up with Building Inspector.
o Public notification must appear in the Berkshire Eagle first notification by May 18th, second
notification May 25th.
Action item Bob Hartt and Jordan Archey to confirm dates for posting with Town Clerk and post.
o Public Hearing will be scheduled on June 1st at 7 p.m. at New Marlborough Fire House.
Action item Christian Stovall to confirm.
o New Warrants must be provided to Select Board and posted by June 10th to meet the 14-day
requirement for Special Town Meeting.
o Date of Special Town Meeting will be clarified by Tara White Select Board depending on School
Committee update.
ADU Bylaw Finalization- requesting confirmation that changes have been made based on Attorney General
feedback and Attorney General has signed of. Changes specific to off street parking and single-family units
have been amended to conform with AG requirements.
Action item- Chair to follow up with Town Administrator about the status of the ADU draft and if Attorney
General has approved.
New Business
Planning Board Composition and Officers- Discussion of Chair and Vice Chair positions. Officer selection is a
standard process after an election of committee members which occurred on May 11th. Chair Bob Hartt
suggested that he remain as Chair for this year (2026) and that Jordan Archey assumes role of Vice Chair. This
change will provide for succession planning and aligns with Jordan’s interest and passion for this work. Plan
will be to vote on these changes at the May 19th Planning Board Meeting.
Action item Chair will speak to Jon James to solicit his input in advance of the May 19th meeting.
Request to standardize the schedule for Planning Board Meetings. Consistent scheduling will allow meetings
to be placed on the Town’s website calendar. Brief discussion of challenges related to summer scheduling.
Action item to be discussed at a future meeting.
Upcoming Meetings
May 19th 6:30 p.m. confirm warrant changes, identify content experts to speak to specific warrant items, and
formalize strategy.
May 26th 6:30 p.m. finalize the revised draft of warrant items specific to specific areas of content.
Adjourned 8:23 p.m.

Egremont Planning Board Minutes
Meeting date: May 18, 2026
Location: Zoom
Chair: Mary McGurn
Board members present: John Lanterman, Donna Bersch-Gordon, Eddie Regandahl, Blake McDonald
Board members absent: Stephen Lyle
Guests: James Pardoe, Mike Parsons, Lucinda Vermeulen, Eileen Vining, Bruce Mallory
Call to Order time: 10:03 AM
Adjournment time: 11:52 AM
Next meeting date/time: Wednesday, June 10, 2026 at 10:00 AM.
Key Outputs with motions and vote results
• Approved the Pardoe Form A / Approval Not Required plan for three lots on Prospect Lake Road.
Motion by John Lanterman; second by Eddie Regandahl; vote: Eddie Regandahl yes, John
Lanterman yes, Donna Bersch-Gordon yes, Mary McGurn yes; outcome: approved.
• Confirmed the Attorney General approved the Town Meeting zoning amendments, including
Article 6 Cottage Cluster Development, and that Article 2 Design Standards required only
deletion of one word, “solely,” as directed.
• Reviewed progress and concerns regarding the short-term rental zoning and general bylaw
package for the June 16, 2026 Special Town Meeting, including parking, resident/owner-
occupied definitions, inactive registrations, and the need for clearer public information.
• Agreed that Mary McGurn and Stephen Lyle may continue as Berkshire Regional Planning
Commission delegate/alternate for FY2027.
• Discussed upcoming applications expected for a Greenagers community/farm event annual
renewable special permit and a possible OxBow Cottage Cluster Development site plan review.
Agenda Item Discussion
Form A: Pardoe
Mike Parsons presented the Form A / Approval Not Required plan on behalf of James Pardoe.
The property is approximately 10.5 acres on the east side of Prospect Lake Road and had previously been
divided into four parcels, but the earlier plan was not recorded at the Registry of Deeds. The current plan
combines those parcels into three lots.
The Board reviewed whether the lots have required frontage, area, and access from Prospect Lake Road.
The stated lot areas were Lot 1: 1.822 acres; Lot 2: 1.606 acres; Lot 3: 6.989 acres. Frontage was stated
as Lot 1: 168.3 feet; Lot 2: 150 feet; Lot 3: 300.02 feet.
Board discussion included possible future common driveway permitting, grading/access from Prospect
Lake Road, mature vegetation, the pond/vernal pool on Lot 3, and potential Conservation Commission
jurisdiction.
James Pardoe stated that the intent is to build a home, raise a family, keep the parcel natural and
consistent with the neighborhood, use the existing driveway through a future common driveway
application, and avoid development near the pond.
Motion by: John Lanterman. Second: Eddie Regandahl. Motion text: “I move to approve the Pardoe
Catahoula LLC Form A as submitted with three lots.” Vote: Eddie Regandahl yes; John Lanterman yes;
Donna Bersch-Gordon yes; Mary McGurn yes. Outcome: approved.
The Chair stated that the Board would arrange for three members to sign the Mylar and copy, and then
notify Mike Parsons’ office when the documents were ready for pickup and recording.
John Lanterman asked to learn more about Form A practice in Massachusetts. Mike Parsons offered to
provide a planner’s handbook on Form A applications and leave it in Planning Board mailbox.
Review and approval of minutes.
No minutes were available for approval.
Report on Attorney General ruling on Article 2 Design Standards and Article 6 Cottage Cluster
Development
The Chair reported that all nine articles adopted at the December 11, 2025 Town Meeting were
approved by the Attorney General, with one exception: the word “solely” in Article 2 Design Standards
was disapproved or required to be struck due to a conflict with state law.
Town Counsel confirmed that the Chair could strike the word from the zoning bylaw text without
returning to Town Meeting.
The corrected zoning bylaw was sent to the Town Clerk and town website as current zoning amended as
of December 11, 2025.
The Chair emphasized that the approval of Article 6 means the Cottage Cluster Development provisions
are now legally effective, which matters for any upcoming OxBow Cottage Cluster Development site plan
review.
Discuss progress on short-term rental bylaws to meet June 16, 2026 Special Town Meeting
The Chair reported that the Planning Board’s short-term rental zoning bylaw, as adopted by the Board at
its prior Thursday meeting, had been checked for typographical and punctuation issues and sent to Mary
Brazie for the Select Board.
Board members and members of the public discussed the separate general bylaw being developed
through the Municipal Housing Trust. Concerns included the number and complexity of definitions, the
proposed 10 percent cap, treatment of inactive short-term rental registrations, and whether the general
bylaw would be understandable on Town Meeting floor.
Donna Bersch-Gordon stated that she supports regulating short-term rentals but was concerned that the
draft general bylaw may be cumbersome and confusing. She also noted that including inactive
registrations in the 10 percent cap could undermine the practical effect of the cap.
John Lanterman stated that the Housing Trust had come a long way and listened to many comments, and
that he generally favored balancing short-term rental interests with affordable housing needs.
Blake McDonald identified two central issues: the resident-only rule for future short-term rental owners
and the townwide 10 percent cap, especially if inactive registrations hold available license slots.
The Board discussed possible amendments from the Town Meeting floor and the possibility that the
Housing Trust might bring clarifying amendments itself. Several speakers supported another public
information session before Special Town Meeting because the general bylaw had changed substantially.
Lucinda stated that an additional informational meeting would be important for the Housing Trust and
the town and said she would mention it at the next Select Board meeting.
Bruce reviewed the Planning Board’s short-term rental infographic and asked about parking. The Chair
explained that the Board had changed the parking requirement to two spaces plus one additional space
and retained the waiver provision. Bruce said that was easier to understand.
The Board noted that the June 16, 2026 Special Town Meeting date still needed Select Board
confirmation.
Berkshire Regional Planning Commission delegate/alternate reappointments: McGurn/Lyle
The Chair explained the role of the Berkshire Regional Planning Commission (BRPC), defining it as a
regional planning agency serving Berkshire County municipalities and describing its municipal
delegate/alternate structure.
The Chair explained that the delegate votes when present and the alternate may attend and vote when
the delegate cannot attend.
The Chair asked whether the Board was comfortable with Mary McGurn and Stephen Lyle continuing for
as delegate and alternate. Donna Bersch-Gordon and John Lanterman thanked them for continuing to
represent the Board. No objection was stated.
The Chair also forwarded information from BRPC about the state rural policy update process, including
webinars on housing, land use, sustainability, technology, and related rural issues. Members were
encouraged to review the email and consider attending relevant webinars.
Donna Bersch-Gordon raised the idea of rural-specific treatment for seasonal housing/cottage cluster
setback requirements. The Chair noted that she had contacted Matt Walsh at the Executive Office of
Housing and Livable Communities (EOHLC) for guidance on compliance with mandatory zoning while
preserving Egremont’s cottage cluster approach.
New business: Expectation of an annual, renewal special permit for a Community/Farm event
(Greenagers)
The Chair reported that Oscar Hallig is coordinating a Greenagers gala event and had contacted her
about site plan requirements.
The event is expected to be the Board’s first application under the new community and farm
event/function us

4/14/26 with the addition of Bonnie’s name in the attendees list via Zoom. The minutes were
Approved by unanimous vote. Schedule of taking meeting minutes: Juliette in June, Sharon in
July, and Marj in August.
Sustainability Report: Juliette reported that she has submitted the RDP Grant application
which is due June 1, 2026. Egremont will receive 12 points or $5200 for the year.
New Business:
“Just Eat It” film at Triplex June 3, 2026, 7:00 pm. Stephanie Blumenthal updated the group
on the upcoming food waste film screening. Stephanie reported that after the film, a
representative from CET (Center for Eco Technology) will speak about what we can do to
combat food waste. In addition, Yoni Auerbach from ReFED, a U.S.-based nonprofit working to
solve food waste, will be in the lobby to answer questions. Tables in the lobby will have
information about what expiration dates really mean, composting, and recipes for using and
preserving food at home to avoid waste. Attendees will be able to taste finger food samples
prepared from the website savethefood. The Triplex will charge $9/person and this is part of the
film series that Stephanie is coordinating. Stephanie will send an announcement/flier to Emily
for distribution via NeighborNet, bulletin boards in town, and the town’s website.
Egremont Green Committee members will prepare and bring food from recipes from
www.savethe food.com. Pat will make Rustic Potato Chips and the Apple Cookies, Marj will
make carrot macaroons, and Sue is making Banana bread. Marj will pick up the food from Pat
and Sue and bring it to the theatre. Emily will help set up and clean up. Juliette and Marj will
coordinate printing copies of the recipes used - at Town Hall and bring them to the event.
Old Business:
April 2026 Roadside Cleanup. Marj reported that we had more than 100 volunteers and all
roads in Egremont were covered. This year there were less pounds of materials collected than
in past years. Marj believes that this is probably due to folks picking up trash and recyclables on
their daily or weekly walks and not waiting for the April event to collect trash. The pizza party at
the Town Hall was great fun and there were about 35-40 people that attended. “Everyone had a
good time” according to Marj. The committee discussed the need to involve younger people and
new volunteers in future events, as the Green Committee members/organizers may choose not to
continue indefinitely.
Microplastics Survey: The Berkshire Regional Planning Commission has offered to create a
survey about community preferences for plastic reduction measures. During the April meeting,
committee members were asked to submit 2-3 possible survey questions. Juliette compiled the
survey questions and sent the Micro Plastic Survey document to the committee for comments.
Sharon and Bonnie had two minor edits and clarifications. Juliette will submit it to the Board of
Health on May 21st for final approval. Juliette will make any edits from the BoH, send it to Aaron
with BRPC for final formatting. Juliette will print hard copies of the survey for distribution in
public spaces. Mary McGurn will create a link/QR code to the survey and place it on the EGC
website and will also send it out via a “News Flash”, NeighborNet, and post on Facebook. Once
the survey is complete, the committee will discuss next steps in reducing plastics use and
microplastic contamination.
Upcoming events: Juliette reported that the October 10th collection event with is scheduled
from 1:00-3:00 PM to align with the Transfer Station’s closing time. Funding will come from the
RDP grant. Additional funding for the shredding will be pursued with NBT (formerly Salisbury
Bank.) and possibly Lee Bank. The event will include shredding with “Pro-Shred”, Freon-
removal by IRRI (Interstate Refrigerant Recovery, Inc) for air conditioners and de-humidifiers,
CMRK for household items, and Bay State Books for book recycling. The committee will invite
Sheffield residents. The committee discussed what other items might be collected at this event.
Bonnie suggested sofas (too large and hard to manage) and electronics. Bonnie suggested
Dream Green Recycling company from Adams, MA who pick up tv’s, electronics, furniture and
other items at your house. They might be able to bring their truck to the October event. The
website is https://www.dreamgreenrecycling.com. Emily suggested bike collection/recycling and
that there was a company in Pittsfield that used to collect bikes for re-use. She will research it.
The next Green Committee meeting is scheduled for June 23, 2026, at 4:30 pm.
The meeting was adjourned at 5:25 PM.
Respectfully submitted,
Bonnie Greenwood

TOWN OF EGREMONT, MASSACHUSETTS
MEETING OF THE SELECT BOARD
MINUTES
******************************************************************************
Date: May 19, 2026
Time: 10:00 A.M.
Place: Via Zoom Meeting & Town Hall
Egremont
Present at the meeting in person were Select Board Chairwoman Lucinda Vermeulen, Vice
Chairwoman Judi Goodman, Board Member Mary Brazie, Administrative Assistant Mindy
Nilson, Clerk/Board of Health Director Juliette Haas, Highway Superintendent Jim Noe, Nate
Mrowka and Cathy O’Malley.
Present via zoom were Mary McGurn, and Grant Administrator Peg McDonough.
The meeting was audio and video recorded.
ACCEPTANCE OF MINUTES:
The minutes of the Select Board meeting from May 5 were accepted with minor edits.
The minutes from the May 5 evening meeting (Prior to the Annual Town meeting) were accepted
as presented.
TOWN OFFICIALS:
Town Clerk Juliette Haas asked to be placed on a future Select Board agenda to discuss
election options. She noted that several issues arose during the recent elections and would like
the Board’s input on possible options for future elections.
SCHEDULED ISSUES:
The Select Board conducted their annual board realignment, electing Lucinda Vermeulen
as chair, Judi Goodman as vice chair, and Mary Brazie as member.
Highway Superintendent Jim Noe appeared before the Select Board regarding the hiring
of Nate Mrowka for the Highway Department CDL position. The Select Board unanimously
approved the request. Nate will begin employment on June 1, 2026.
NEW BUSINESS:
The Select Board approved a one day beer and wine special license for Greenagers'
annual gala on August 14th from 5 p.m. to 10 p.m.
OLD BUSINESS:
The Select Board discussed the upcoming Special Town Meeting scheduled for June.
After discussion, the Board finalized the date as June 29, 2026, at 6:00 PM, to be held at Mount
Everett Regional School.
The Select Board discussed the short term rental by-law that is already on the warrant for
the June special town meeting. Lucinda expressed concern about the by-law's potential to fail due
to public pushback, despite the Housing Trust incorporating many suggestions, and suggested
having one more informational meeting.
The Select Board also reviewed the warrant articles, including a correction needed to
transfer $40,000 from overlay surplus rather than free cash, and discussed the order of articles
with the zoning bylaw potentially coming first followed by the short-term rental bylaws. The
meeting also addressed concerns about the bylaw process and public engagement. The
discussion concluded with concerns about assessor certifications, particularly regarding new
assessor Richard Allen who needs to complete his certification through the Gateway system to
address compliance issues raised by the Department of Revenue. Mary Brazie will reach out to
Francine to confirm her willingness to be reappointed temporarily as a signatory-only assessor.
GRANTS:
Grant Administrator Peg McDonough provided updates on several grant applications,
including a potential MassDOT Community Culvert Grant for $1 million and a new Mass COA
Transportation grant for $25,000 to expand the Tri-Town Connector service. The Select Board
discussed the need for better tracking of grant applications and administration, with Lucinda
requesting a spreadsheet to follow the progress of various grants. Mary Brazie also mentioned
considering whether Berkshire Regional Planning Commission could assist with grant
administration.
SELECT BOARD ITEMS:
Next meeting: June 4, 2026 @ 9:30am
Adjournment 10:50 am
Mindy Nilson
Administrative Assistant
