for the Working Group, and a related list of mandates or responsibilities for the group. Tara emphasized
that the transfer station mission statement should be short and suitable for public posting, while the
working group mission statement and mandate are separate documents that describe the group’s role and
responsibilities in more detail. The group agreed that the two mission statements and mandate should be
sent to the Select Board for review, comment, and approval.
3. Station Communications and Signage
Gardiner presented an overview of the station’s current communications and signage, noting that
information now reaches residents through several channels and is not always consistent or clear. He
emphasized the need for signage that is simpler and less negative in tone. He recommended a short-term
effort to remove confusing or outdated signs and add temporary signs where needed, followed by a longer-
term signage plan coordinated with the site redesign. The long-term goal would be a station-wide system of
permanent signs with consistent design and accurate instructions. The broader goal would be a more
welcoming station identity, including possible use of a logo, gear, and other cues that support respect for
attendants and their role. Gardiner said he would like to take the lead on this work. Freddy and Marc
expressed support for the plan.
4. Site Rework and Engineering Update
Marc reported that Mike Kulig’s topographic survey work is done, though the container layout and swap
shop location still need to be added. Marc said he plans to meet Mike at the station to walk the site, clarify
the container area, and review traffic-flow options. Marc also talked with Joe Wilkinson to confirm that his
proposed excavation fee was unchanged. Joe indicated that a fuel surcharge would be added.
Several possible swap shed locations were discussed, including the inbound area, the center of the station,
the container area, or possibly inside a container itself. Wherever it lands, the group agreed the swap shed
may require either an attendant presence or a volunteer system to prevent it from becoming an
unmanaged dumping area. The group agreed that options should be reviewed on site before any final
decision is made.
5. Point-of-Sale System and Other Updates
Marc updated the group on the point-of-sale payment system, which should help attendants calculate and
record fees, support several payment methods including cash, checks, Venmo, and credit cards, and make it
easier to determine charges. Tara pointed out that the town would not absorb electronic payment fees.
Marc described the test “sandbox” system he has set up. He said the app has been configured, the back end
is complete, and the financial systems have been tested. Next steps are to complete a full test transaction
with Finance, demonstrate the system to the group, and equip and train attendants for a possible mid-July
launch. Needed equipment includes printers and phones or tablets for attendants.
Marc also described potential tools for estimating bulky-waste volume and posting swap-shop items online.
The group was generally interested in exploring these ideas. Marc noted that the bulky-waste estimator
could free attendants from guesswork. Chuck commented that even if the waste-volume app worked, some
residents could be expected to challenge its estimates.
6. Job Descriptions and Staffing
The group decided to postpone discussion of the revised attendant job description, which Gardiner had
circulated before the meeting but which still requires final group review. The group agreed to revisit the job
description at the next meeting and then forward a finalized version for Select Board review.
A motion was made and seconded to adjourn. The meeting adjourned at 12:03 p.m.

TOWN OF NEW MARLBOROUGH
PB Public Meeting
June 1st, 2026
Approved
Meeting convened 7:05 p.m.
Attendees:
 Planning Board Committee: Bob Hartt Chair, Jordan Archey Vice Chair, Jon
James, Christian Stovall, Becky Wilkinson, Jennie Wright Secretary.
 Municipal leads- Select Board Maggie Arian and Tara White, Town Administrator
Mari Enoch, Town Counsel Jeremia Pollard, Building Inspector Matthew Kollmer
 Public attending 55 in person and 4 virtually.
Chair opened the meeting providing context and history on the reason for and process
of Protective Bylaw recodification (reorganization) and changes. This was possible due
to New Marlborough obtaining grant funding through Berkshire Regional Planning
Commission (BRPC). BRPC undertook this work and these recodification and changes
were presented as warrant items at the Annual Town Meeting (ATM) last month.
Warrant 37 recodification was approved. Warrant 38 proposed changes to align with
current state building code, agricultural provisions and case law did not receive two
thirds of the necessary votes. An upcoming Special Town Meeting (STM) is scheduled
at the end of June. Planning Board’s goal of aligning Protective Bylaws with existing
code and law expediently and plans on presenting the contents of the revised Warrant
38 creating articles relevant to three distinct categories-
(1) Bylaw changes requested by our Building Inspector to align with the July 2025
Building Code.
(2) General Administrative Bylaw clarifications including municipal and private
service buildings.
(3) Articles recommended by Town Counsel including 1) clarification that cannabis
cultivation is not included as agriculture. 2) Approval of language to align with
Attorney General’s recommendations on our current Accessory Dwelling Unit
(ADU) bylaw.
The goal of the public hearing is to provide an updated version of Protective Bylaw
changes to the community. Providing legal rationale and solicit feedback which the
Planning Board will review and consider. The Chair acknowledged suggestions for
establishing a committee to review current zoning, noting this is out of scope for this
meeting and these articles, but can be future agenda items.
Building Bylaw Changes and Special Permits. Vice Chair Jordan Archey led this
discussion with input from Matthew Kollmer and Jeremia Pollard.
 Building permit approval- adjusting bylaw with practice, BI approves as opposed
to Select Board.
 Building permit valid 180 days to align with other local communities.
 Dwelling Unit definition to align with changes recommended by the BI to comply
with state building code.
 Variance allowance 2 years, BI recommends two years to align with other local
communities. Clarification that a variance is a special permit which grants
authority to vary from existing law.
 Special permit- two years versus one year will be changed to align with
comments.
 Table to demonstrating what is allowed “by right”, “special permit”, “not allowed”.
Will be attached as an addendum.
Special Permit Rural District Slaughterhouse. Discussion then moved to
slaughterhouse/meat processing facility. PB clarified that this be considered by special
permit and only in rural districts. Both a mobile and brick and mortar facility would
require a special permit. It was noted that while it is unlikely to occur in New
Marlborough, there is value in remaining open to this possibility as currently it is
challenging for local farmers to go out of state. Clarification by residents regarding
processing of poultry versus beef, processing for personal versus commercial sale.
Three slaughterhouses in the state of MA noted to be large facilities with USDA
oversight.
SB member Maggie Arian reviewed the requirements in applying for and obtaining a
special permit. Chair Bob Hartt reinforced that a special permit promotes community
discussion.
Separation of Cannabis Cultivation from Agricultural Use. Town Counsel reviewed
a case which has encouraged communities to exclude cannabis cultivation from
agricultural use.
Municipal and Service Building Use- is already in the existing bylaw and PB has
updated this version.
Agricultural Use Right to Farm Jordan Archey recused herself and Christian Stovall
facilitated. Robust discussion around agricultural use and clarification of what is
included in the Right to Farm Bylaw. This bylaw was adopted in 2006 and passed at the
Annual Town Meeting (ATM) that year. Town Counsel clarified that greenhouses, fur
farms (of which the state has none), and farm animals including horses, cattle and
pigs/swine are already protected if the owner has a 5 acre or larger property. This is
existing state law and has been validated in MA case law. He reinforced that the bylaw
changes are to comply with MA state law.
Brief discussion related to piggeries with redirection of options for concerned residents
to bring concerns to the New Marlborough Board of Health.
Clarifications and Suggestions by Attendees
1) By defining agricultural use PB is eliminating exclusion of piggeries and fur
farming- to be consistent with Right to Farm.
2) Suggestion to clarify 5 acres or more to be consistent with 40A.
3) Noted by attendee that agricultural use 40A section 3 (state right to farm) has
been revised by the state to allow 2 acres with income generation of $1,000 per
acre demonstrated to the state. Town Counsel agreed.
4) Agricultural use 40A section 3- this law covers fur farming, commercial
greenhouses, horses and all livestock - including pigs.
5) Fur farming- no fur farms in MA. Town Counsel and PB chair noted need to
conform with state law as this is still included.
6) Removing commercial greenhouse language- greenhouses are also included in
Agricultural use and this will reduce confusion.
7) Board of Health may want to create recommendations related to water quality.
8) Signage display noted in Section 5.3 and 5.2 Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU).
Discussion that many small business owners have vehicles displaying their
business (signage) and that ADU language currently prohibits. Town Counsel
validated this concern noting it has been identified in other communities as
problematic as work vehicles could be considered signage. Town Counsel
explained that the goal is to prevent large commercial operations in a residential
area, it does create issues for small business owners who park at their homes.
PB Vice Chair suggests that this be taken into consideration for review.
9) Banning AI facility development also taken into consideration for 2027.
Planning Board thanked those attending for their suggestions and feedback and
updated the group of review of these suggestions at an upcoming Planning Board
meeting.
Meeting adjourned 8:10 p.m.

Tara B. White called the meeting to order at 5:00pm.
Pledge of Allegiance and Moment of Silence for Veterans
The Pledge of Allegiance was recited and a moment of silence for Veterans was held.
Hear updates from Construct RE Cassilis Housing Project
Three members of Construct, Inc. were present to discuss the status of the Cassilis renovation project.
Tara White explained that some residents were concerned about the appearance of the Cassilis property,
noting that the fence was removed. Executive Director Joey Lindstrom explained that the fence was
removed because it was costly, not attractive, and did not provide much security. He wondered if
installing a sign in front of the house would make it clear that the work is ongoing. Joey went on to say
that the demolition phase cost more and took longer than expected, somewhat due to the discovery of
asbestos. He said they had to reevaluate the budget and brought on a new construction team, Allegrone. In
addition, he mentioned changes in the design concept, substantial increases in development costs and a
financing gap. He was hopeful that they could reduce that gap to about $350,000 after government
assistance, and are approaching various organizations for assistance.
1
Joey requested that New Marlborough support the project in any of three ways: 1) submit an application
to the Small Town Development Program for further grant funding, 2) reduce or waive fees for building
permits, 3) provide relief in the Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT) agreement.
Tara asked when work will commence and was informed that Construct hoped to have the final funding
secured next fall. The project completion is projected for the fall of 2027. James Blake said that
construction could begin immediately, once the funding is secured, and it will not be impacted by winter
weather. A new well needs be drilled, to be used in addition to the existing water source. Once the buffer
zone is established, the remainder of the adjoining vacant parcel will be purchased by an abutter.
John Schreiber, speaking to the Historic Demolition Pause bylaw, asked about permitting for the
relocation of the milk house building, and potential demolition of the barns. Joey said moving the small
building is still in the works with the buyer. If it is deemed not possible, the purchaser may consider her
payment a donation and leave it standing. Mike Howard said demolishing or auctioning off the two large
barns is still an option and no decisions had been made.
Tara said the PILOT agreement for FY 24-26 expires on 6/30/26 and needs to be renegotiated.
The current three year agreement calls for Construct to pay $2,991.44. per year, for a total of $8,974.32
deferred until 90 days after final Certificate of Occupancy is issued. Joey will email Mari with any
requests from Construct, Inc. for the PILOT extension.
In regards to the upcoming Small Town Development Program grant, Joey said his staff will prepare the
application and the request will be around $100,000. The application is due June 3rd. Mari asked the
Board to vote on authorizing her to submit the application for the housing grant and sign a letter of
support.
Tara made a motion, Maggie seconded, and it was so voted to authorize Mari to submit an
application for the Rural and Small Town Development Grant Program for New Marlborough, for
an amount up to $300,000 for the Cassilis Farm project.
Tara B. White Aye
Bill West Aye
Maggie Arian Aye
Appoint Designer Selection Committee
Tara said P3 was chosen as the Project Manager of the Town Hall renovation, and a committee is needed
to review proposals and choose a designer. Mari said qualifications from architects are due by Wednesday
6/10/26 at 2pm. Those proposals will be reviewed by the committee.
A call for volunteers was issued by the town and four letters of interest were submitted by Mark Carson,
Chuck Loring, Barbara Marchione and Bob Hartt. The fifth member will be a member of the Select
Board. As Chief Procurement Officer, Mari will attend meetings as a liaison for the project.
Tara made a motion, Bill seconded, and so voted to appoint Mark Carson, Chuck Loring, Barbara
Marchione, Bob Hartt and Maggie Arian (Select Board representative) to the Designer
Selection/Design Review Committee for the duration of the project.
Tara B. White Aye
Bill West Aye
Maggie Arian Aye
2
Hear request from New Marlborough Historical Society regarding Town Hall space
John Schreiber was present on behalf of the New Marlborough Historical Society to request that the town
hall renovation plans include a dedicated space in the Town Hall to house historic New Marlborough
artifacts. The items belong to the private Historical Society but he hoped that because they benefit the
Town an arrangement could be made to keep them in Town Hall where they are currently stored. He had
explored the possibility of the Historical Society buying the old Grange Hall in Hartsville but the asking
price was $250,000. Tara explained that they cannot guarantee a dedicated space in the new plans as the
programming hadn’t been finalized yet. Mari said they need to know how much display space and how
much storage space is being requested. John will get back to Mari.
Review and take action on Order of Taking for Reconstruction of Canaan-Southfield Road culvert
Mari explained that Town Counsel will record an Order of Taking for the reconstruction of the culvert on
Canaan Southfield Road. There are two property owners involved. Tonight, the Select Board will vote on
the permanent and temporary easements located on the Goodnow property. The permanent easement is
for 3,080 square feet and the temporary easement is for 949 square feet. The Goodnow family has
donated the easements. The Board thanked the Goodnows for their donation and for the long history of
cooperation and generosity with the town on various projects. The Board will vote on the second Order of
Taking at another time.
Tara made a motion, Maggie seconded, and so voted to sign the Order of Talking for the
permanent and temporary easement on the Goodnow property for the reconstruction of the
Canaan-Southfield Rd. culvert.
Tara B. White Aye
Bill West Aye
Maggie Arian Aye
Review and take action on Town Counsel Contact Policy
Tara read the proposed Town Counsel Contact Policy, which specifies the only officials and
employees who are authorized to reach out directly to the town’s legal counsel. The list is as
follows: Select Board members, Town Administrator, Town Clerk, Board of Assessors/Assistant
Assessor, Planning Board Chair, Conservation Commission Chair, and Board of Health Chair.
Mari said that Town Counsel will not respond to anyone other than those listed in the policy.
Should other officials need to speak to Town Counsel, they should go through the Town
Administrator or a Select Board member. This will ensure efficient operations, consistent legal
guidance, and responsible management of legal costs for the Town of New Marlborough.
Tara made a motion, Maggie seconded it, and it was so voted to adopt the policy for contact
with Town Counsel as read.

Tara B. White called the meeting to order at 6:00 pm.
Pledge of Allegiance and Moment of Silence for Veterans
The Pledge of Allegiance was recited and a moment of silence for Veterans was held.
Hearing for National Grid Pole Permits:
a. North Road from the intersection of Old North Road approximately 2,650’ east (19
Poles)
Steven Hayward from National Grid requested permission to install 8 brand new poles and 11
replacements on North Road between house numbers 405 and 390 to extend electrical service to house
#390. As there is currently no electrical service on that section of road, the proposal is for the 11
replacement poles to replace the poles currently owned by Fiber Connect that carry its broadband wires.
The plan will be to install the replacement poles behind or adjacent to existing Fiber Connect poles.
National Grid would like Fiber Connect to connect to its poles and then the Fiber Connect poles will be
removed.
1
The 8 new poles will be installed in locations where the distance between existing poles is too
great to adequately support the electrical wires. After meeting with an abutter, Mr. Hayward stated he
made a slight change to the location of proposed pole 42. He said he is working with the New
Marlborough Tree Warden and Highway Department to address tree trimming. National Grid was
encouraged to remove the dead ash trees when it trims. The expected duration of the pole installation is a
few weeks. The Board asked Adam Chait if Fiber Connect had worked out an agreement with National
Grid. Adam said he was just hearing about the proposal today, but the hope is that he would attach to
National Grid poles and then remove his poles. He noted the details had to be worked out. There would be
no double poles. Mari reiterated that Town’s request that the National Grid poles be no closer to the road
than the current Fiber Connect poles. If possible, the replacement poles should be in back of the current
poles. Steven said the total installation time will be a few weeks. Tara suggested the Board hold off on
approving the pole permit until an agreement is made between Fiber Connect and National Grid. The
Board expects to revisit the application at its next meeting on June 22.
b. Canaan Southfield Road at approximately 108 New Marlborough Southfield Road (1
pole)
Tara White read the request from National Grid to install one new pole for a new residence on New
Marlborough Southfield Rd.
Tara made a motion, Maggie seconded, and it was so voted to approve the permit for National Grid
to install a pole located at 108 New Marlborough Southfield Rd.
Tara B. White Aye
Bill West Aye
Maggie Arian Aye
Review and take action on proposed revisions for Building Department Fees
Building Commissioner Matt Kollmer provided the proposed list of updated Building Department fees.
Since New Marlborough is now part of the regional building department, there is a desire to standardize
fees across all participating towns. The new fees include a $20.00 filing fee per application. The Board
reviewed the fees and received clarifications on questions.
Matt also provided an update on changes to the regional Building Department. As of July 1, New
Marlborough’s local building inspector will likely be Keith Gangell, who will be shared with Great
Barrington. Jessie Self will be the first point of contact and administrative support also out of the Great
Barrington office. Matt confirmed that New Marlborough residents can access building department staff
at the building office in the Great Barrington Town Hall and he will send contact information to Mari.
Tara made a motion, Maggie seconded and so voted to adopt the new Building Department fee
schedule, which will go into effect on July 1, 2026.
Tara B. White Aye
Bill West Aye
Maggie Arian Aye
Review and sign Special Town Meeting warrant for June 29, 2026
Tara explained that the warrant is not complete yet. The Planning Board will meet this week to finalize its
proposed zoning bylaw amendments to be included in the warrant.
Mari mentioned that the warrant will include the Southern Berkshire Regional School District assessment
which was recently adopted 9-0 by the SBRSD school committee. Also on the warrant will be a proposed
2
bylaw authorizing the Conservation Commission to implement a fee schedule. The Planning Board will
also propose zoning amendments.
Review and sign amendment to agreement with Southern Berkshire Ambulance Inc for Paramedic
Intercept
Tara read the letter from Southern Berkshire Ambulance, Inc. to Chief Medical Officer Maureen Krejci,
which revises the Reciprocal Backup and Paramedic Intercept Agreement. Due to high costs, SBA is
requesting an increase to the flat fee from $285.00 to $400.00 per paramedic intercept.
Tara made a motion, Maggie seconded, and it was voted to accept Amendment #1 to the Reciprocal
Backup and Paramedic Intercept Agreement with Southern Berkshire Ambulance, Inc.
Tara B. White Aye
Bill West Aye
Maggie Arian Aye
Review and approve grant application for 2027 MRS Police grant
The Police Dept. requested permission to apply for a grant in the amount of $12,880. Tara explained that
this grant is for radar speed signs and overtime patrol, and there is no match required. The date of the
original agreement is 9/19/25.
Tara made a motion, Maggie seconded, and it was so voted to accept grant application and
authorize Mari Enoch to sign and approve the grant application request in the amount of
$12,880.00
Tara B. White Aye
Bill West Aye
Maggie Arian Aye
Town Administrator Updates
Mari provided an update from MASS DOT that the Town was awarded a grant in the amount of $489,000
to repair the Campbell Falls Road keystone bridge over the Whiting River. The design has been
completed and permitting is in process. Gill Engineering assisted in the application of this grant.
The Fire Department was awarded a grant from Mass Department of Conservation and Recreation (DCR)
for 18 sets of protective gear to fight brush fires. It is a matching grant in the amount of $3,105.00 in FY
27. The match will come out of the fire department budget. She thanked John Halbreich for his work on
this grant.
Board of Selectmen Updates
Tara said the Designer Selection Committee will have its first meeting tomorrow. Proposals from 5
architects were received and the committee will review and evaluate the proposals.
Administrative: Payroll and Vendor Warrants, Business Licenses
Payroll and vendor warrants were signed.
Review and approve minutes of previous meetings
None.

Keith Wilkinson was present to ask if there is an update on dust control on the dirt roads. He would like
to have this matter added to the next Select Board agenda.
3
He also asked about office hours for the Building Inspector in New Marlborough. Mari said residents are
welcome to contact the Building Dept. to request a meeting in New Marlborough, however the Town is
now part of a regional department that has centralized offices in Great Barrington and Lee.
Adjourn
Being that there was no further business to be brought before the Board, a motion was made by
Tara, seconded by Bill, and it was so voted to adjourn the meeting at 7:26 pm.
Tara B. White Aye

Housing Trust Board
June 9, 2026, 8:00 AM
Present at Town Hall were members Mary Brazie, Judi Goodman, Doug Mishkin and
Evan Hardcastle, as well as Planning Board member John Lanterman.
Present via zoom were Chair Richard Stanley and Planning Board member Mary
McGurn.
The meeting was audio and video recorded.
The group approved meeting minutes from April 28, April 29, May 1, May 12, and May 15.
It was noted that work on the CDC Workforce Housing Project has begun and there was
recently a groundbreaking event.
Short-Term Rental Bylaw Changes
The group discussed proposed changes to a bylaw regarding short-term rentals and
inactive registrations. Judy proposed adding a sentence to section 24.4C requiring trustees
and LLC members to be natural persons, not corporations. The team debated the
registration process for inactive short-term rentals, particularly whether properties must be
registered with the state before the bylaw's effective date. They considered simplifying the
language to clarify that registering with the state preserves the right to operate as an
inactive short-term rental without being subject to the cap. The group also discussed
potentially deleting section 24.4D entirely and incorporating the fee exemption for inactive
rentals into section 24.4C.
The group discussed the definition and registration requirements for inactive short-term
rentals, deciding to remove sections A and B from the definition while keeping section C
intact. They agreed to add language specifying that an inactive short-term rental must
register with both the Commonwealth and the town to become active. The discussion also
touched on clarifying that owners with multiple existing short-term rentals can continue
operating them, with the only change being the 150-night limitation for whole-house rentals
after the two-year mark.
The group discussed the requirements for short-term rental owners under sectioni 24.6,
focusing on how to handle current and future operations. They debated whether to allow
corporations to continue operating existing short-term rentals, with Egremont expressing
concern about potential legal liability for the town if they banned corporate owners. The
discussion highlighted the need to carefully draft language distinguishing between current
and future operations while avoiding potential lawsuits from property owners.
The group discussed clarifying language around short-term rental registrations in the bylaw,
specifically regarding existing properties like Blake's. The team debated how to phrase the
language around re-registration with the Commonwealth and town registration, with
Richard suggesting using clear distinctions between state and town registrations. They
worked on refining section 24.4 to ensure that currently registered properties could
continue operating as they are, while new registrations would be limited to one property per
owner after the effective date.
The group discussed other concerns with the draft bylaw such as registration fees and
making the document a "living" policy that can evolve with changing needs. They debated
the current $400 and $300 registration fee structure, with Mary Brazy supporting the
existing amounts as reasonable compared to other town fees, while others suggested
potentially lowering them. The team agreed to include language recognizing "the evolving
needs of the town" in the bylaw's purpose statement, and Mary committed to distributing
the revised warrant the following day for the Select Board's signature by tomorrow, with
posting scheduled for Thursday morning.
The group discussed an ambiguity in the bylaw regarding short-term rental status, whether
it belongs to the property or the operator. Mary McGurn proposed adding a non-
transferability provision to clarify that short-term rental registrations are personal to the
registered owner and terminate upon any transfer of ownership. The group agreed to add
this language as section 24.4J, with the current owner eligibility language to be modified in
section 24.4A.
The group scheduled their next meeting for June 23rd at 7:30 AM to finalize plans for
presenting the bylaw changes at the June 29 town meeting. Doug will draft and FAQ and
explanatory document.
Meeting adjourned at 9:16am.
Mary Brazie,
Recording Secretary

The Committee members introduced themselves. Dan Pallota, of P3, has been hired by the
Town as the Owner’s Project Manager for the Town Hall renovation. He will assist the
Committee during the Designer Selection Process. Mari will take minutes and handle
administrative tasks as the Chief Procurement Officer.
Organize Committee

Upon a motion by Mark, seconded by Maggie, Barbara was elected Vice-Chair of the
Committee.
Review and evaluate proposal received in response to Request for Proposals for Designer
Services
Dan explained to the Committee that the Town has funding for the first two phases of the
renovation—designer selection/schematic design and design development. The chosen architect
will be asked to provide 50% Construction Documents and cost estimates as part of Phase I and
II. The fee for Phase I and II is not to exceed $225,000. The anticipated timeline calls for
seeking voter approval for construction funding at a Town Meeting next spring. Dan explained
the RFQ process and scoring based on the criteria published in the RFQ. The selection of the
designer is not based on price but on qualifications. He confirmed that the RFQ was advertised
in the Berkshire Eagle, the Central Register, and CommBuys. An optional walk through was
held on May 18 and an addendum was issued on May 21. The Town received five responses by
the due date of June 3. The responses are from:
SSV Architects, Westborough; Jablonski Devriese, Springfield; ndp, Boston; Clark Green + Bek,
Gt. Barrington, and EDM Studio, Unionville, CT.
Dan confirmed that all five responses met the minimum qualifications and included the correct
paperwork and signed forms.
The Committee members had all individually reviewed the proposals prior to the meeting. As a
group, the members reviewed each proposal and came to a consensus on the scoring based on the
comparative criteria published in the RFQ.

SSV Architects 16

ndp, 17

Studio. Dan will provide interview questions and committee members can submit questions to
Dan through Mari. Questions will be agreed upon by the committee. The interview date is
tentatively set for Tuesday, June 23 beginning at 3:00.

Transfer Station Working Group
June 11, 2026 Minutes approved 7-9-26
The meeting was called to order at 3:30 p.m. at Town Hall. Present were Freddy Friedman, Tara
White, Marc Trachtenberg, and Gardiner Morse. Chuck Loring joined at approximately 3:35.
Agenda: 1) Review and approve minutes; 2) Finalize attendant job descriptions; 3) Transfer station
redesign update; 4) Point-of-sale hardware; 5) Container purchase; 6) Communications update; 7)
Other business.
Approval of Minutes
A motion was made and seconded to approve the prior meeting minutes, with Tara abstaining. The
motion passed.
Attendant Job Descriptions
The group reviewed the draft job description for Transfer Station attendants, with discussion
focused on distinguishing the general responsibilities shared by both attendants from additional
responsibilities assigned to Attendant 1. The group agreed that Attendant 1 should be primarily
responsible for collecting fees while preserving some flexibility for other fee-collection
arrangements as the point-of-sale system develops. Scheduling of hauling and staffing was
identified as an Attendant 1 responsibility. Language referencing OSHA and MassDEP standards will
be simplified to refer more generally to compliance with town policy and applicable rules. Gardiner
will revise the job description as discussed and forward to Mari Enoch who, after review, will send it
to the Select Board.
The group also discussed training, accident reporting, the need for a simple process or form for
documenting injuries and property damage, and the possible placement of an AED at the station.
Transfer Station Redesign
Marc reported on discussions with Mike Kulig regarding the station redesign. The current concept
avoids disturbing the capped landfill area while widening the turning area for hauling and adding fill
as needed to bring the grade up. Marc said that Roger Trucking was happy with the plan. Mike will
prepare a more detailed drawing with grade lines and to help stake the proposed layout on site. The
group discussed how excavation, fill, and concrete blocks would be handled, including whether the
town should purchase certain materials directly through existing town accounts.
Point-of-Sale Hardware
Marc reviewed proposed hardware purchases for the point-of-sale system, including two
phone/tablet devices and a portable cordless receipt printer which could be bought on eBay as
refurbished or open-box equipment at a substantial discount.
Draft - June 11, 2026 TSWG
Container Purchase
The group discussed the planned container configuration and a pending grant request. Tara said
that a grant application had been filed, with a maximum potential award of $8,000, enough to cover
two containers. The grant decision is expected in the fall.
Marc reported that current spot pricing for side-opening containers with roll-up doors is favorable
and may be locked in without immediate purchase or obligation. The group discussed the risk of
jeopardizing grant eligibility by appearing to order the containers before the grant is awarded.
Communications and Signage
Gardiner reviewed the broader communications purpose of the station’s signage and public-facing
messages, noting that signs, attendant interactions, the physical appearance of the station, and
public notices all support the station’s mission by encouraging residents’ compliance with station
rules. The group discussed the need to post Spanish-language signage that’s consistent with the
station’s English signage. Tara noted that the town can receive “points” or payments from MassDEP
for posting multilingual signs. Gardiner proposed posting a limited number of multilingual signs and
directing residents to translation tools or attendants for help. The discussion turned to the station’s
appearance, including cleanup around the sheds and the need to keep public-facing areas orderly.
Freddy updated the group on the recently received metal signs. Some are oversized and may need
to be mounted on bases.
Other Business
The group discussed keeping residents out of the metal container and considered additional signage
or locking options. Members also discussed how long items should remain outside the Swap Shop or
near the metal container before being discarded. Tara will take the lead on helping attendants track
when items should be retained or discarded, including the idea of a color-coded tagging system.
Marc said that the station’s camera system includes an incident function that can preserve relevant
footage beyond the normal 30-day retention period if needed. The group noted that this should be
part of staff training, particularly for accident reporting.
Marc also reported that a town resident with software development experience has offered to help
build a load-measurement app for the station. The group discussed potential conflict-of-interest and
ownership issues if the app were later commercialized. Marc will prepare a written description of
the proposal so it can be reviewed by Mari Enoch, the Select Board, and town counsel as needed.
Adjournment
With no further business, the meeting was adjourned at 5:05 p.m.
Action Items
Draft - June 11, 2026 TSWG
 Develop a simple accident/incident reporting process for station staff (not assigned?)
 Develop a system to help attendants manage items left for reuse or disposal. (Tara)
 Revise attendant job descriptions and forward to Mari/Select Board. (Gardiner)
 Propose signage and other methods to prevent unauthorized access to the metals container.
(Gardiner)
 Add camera incident-retention procedures to staff training. (Marc)
 Write up the proposed load-measurement app and ownership concept and send to the Select
Board and town counsel. (Marc)
 Send the agreed container layout to Mike Kulig. (Marc)
 Send point-of-sale hardware links and purchase details to Tara for approval and copy Jennifer.
(Marc)

******************************************************************************
Date: June 16, 2026
Time: 10:00 A.M.
Place: Via Zoom Meeting & Town Hall
Egremont
Present at the meeting in person were Select Board Chairwoman Lucinda Vermeulen, Vice
Chairwoman Judi Goodman, Board Member Mary Brazie, Administrative Assistant Mindy
Nilson, and Town Clerk/Board of Health Director Juliette Haas.
Present via zoom was Mary McGurn, Peg McDonough, and Marj Wexler.
The meeting was audio and video recorded.
ACCEPTANCE OF MINUTES:
The minutes of the June 3 and June 4 meetings were accepted as presented.
NEW BUSINESS:
The request to use the Town property for firearms certification discussion was deferred.
The Select Board discussed election location concerns, where Town Clerk Juliette Haas
presented issues with holding elections at the North Egremont Firehouse garage, including poor
lighting, heating problems, noise disruption, and safety concerns with the entry ramp. The Select
Board discussed the limited options for election locations, with Town Hall being the only viable
alternative, the Select Board agreed.
The Board of Health Director, Juliette Haas, appeared before the Select Board to discuss an
increase in mattress recycling fees. The fee charged by Tough Stuff Recycling has risen from $33
to $40 per unit, and the Select Board unanimously voted to approve the increase accordingly.
Marj Wexler, representing the Green Committee, proposed collecting redeemable bottles and
cans at the transfer station, with proceeds benefitting Blue Rider Stables. Mary explained that
legal restrictions prohibit collecting redemption proceeds at the public transfer station, or any
Town property. The Select Board voted against allowing the collection program at that location.
The Select Board approved three interdepartmental fund transfers totaling $10,600 to cover
unexpected expenses in computer software, telephone charges, and electric utilities.
The Select Board reviewed annual reappointments and discussed the need to fill positions for
Emergency Management Coordinator and Public Information Officer with questions remaining
about whether Laura Allen wants to be reappointed to the Open Space and Rec Plan Review
Committee. The Select Board approved most positions with the exception of the Emergency
Management Director position which will be left open for now.
The Select Board addressed Peg McDonough’s retirement as grant administrator, and the need to
find a replacement. They discussed exploring options for a new grant administrator, including
potentially working with Berkshire Regional Planning Commission (BRPC) or hiring an
independent contractor. They agreed to prioritize finding a dedicated grant administrator to
handle future applications and ensure existing grants are managed properly.
There was a lengthy discussion regarding the Web Administration and the role this position will
take on moving forward. The Select Board discussed Mary McGurn’s role and budget allocation
after July 1st, when her regular paycheck will end. They determined that she needs to provide a
detailed list of her current duties and responsibilities before the 30th to help determine how to
adjust her hours to fit within the $32,000 budgeted amount. The Board agreed to continue paying
Mary McGurn at her current rate for the two weeks between now and July 14th, when they will
finalize a new plan for her role.
OLD BUSINESS:
The MRF recyclables disposal location discussion with the Board of Health Director
Juliette Haas has been tabled.
June 29, 2026 is the Special Town Meeting to be held at Mount Everett school at 6:00PM
The Select Board will meet to hold a quick meeting prior to the start of the STM at 5:30PM.
GRANTS:
The Grant Administrator Peg McDonough had no updates regarding the grants. All grant
submissions are in and pending or nearing completion.

Housing Trust Board
June 23, 2026, 7:30 AM
Present at Town Hall were Chairman Richard Stanley, members Mary Brazie, Judi Goodman,
Doug Mishkin and Evan Hardcastle . Present via zoom were Mary McGurn and Peg
McDonough.
The meeting was audio and video recorded.
The group approved meeting minutes from June 9.
CDC Housing Project
The board discussed updates on CDC's workforce housing project, where one person who had
responded to the initial inquiry and is moving forward with financing. A significant challenge
emerged regarding the 80% AMI rental unit requirement under 40B, which must be placed in the
statewide lottery, involving potential costs of $15,000 for proper implementation.
There is a question regarding tax assessment issues involving town-owned land being leased for
development projects. Clarity is needed regarding the land which is town-owned while the
homes will be sold and will be taxable.
Housing Trust Short-term Rental Initiative Preparation Discussion
The Board discussed preparations for an upcoming town meeting regarding a housing trust
initiative. There has been some concern expressed about public misunderstanding of the
definition of "persons" and corporate ownership restrictions, but remained confident based on
previous successful town votes on housing matters. The discussion focused on addressing
common questions and concerns raised in public feedback, with it being emphasized that most
issues had already been considered and addressed in the proposal, including limitations on short-
term rentals and accommodations for existing property owners.
Challenges of addressing housing affordability and community development were discussed,
emphasizing the difficulty of quantifying intangible benefits like a diverse economic community.
The focus is be on restricting short-term rentals in properties valued at $500,000 or below to
prevent them from being converted into short-tern housing. The importance of implementing
restrictions to balance housing needs with community goals was stressed.
While some community members want to maintain the ability to use their properties as short-
term rentals, the focus should be on balancing this with the need for affordable housing for
essential workers like nurses and teachers. It was emphasized that while property owners may
potentially make less money from selling their homes under these regulations, such sacrifices are
necessary for the public good to ensure future generations can live in the community.
It was noted there is a possibility that the two-thirds majority required for the zoning bylaw
might not be achieved. If this is the case the general bylaw will not be acted on.
Community Preservation Committee Planning Meeting
The Community Preservation Committee will meet again on July 1st and begin soliciting
applications for CPA funds in the fall. Doug explained that the committee plans to allocate at
least 10% of CPA funds to open space, recreation, historic preservation, and affordable housing,
with the remaining funds to be distributed to relevant boards and committees. The Housing Trust
plans to develop a process for public input on how CPA money should be used, with an expected
application deadline around November 1st.
Grant Opportunities Discussion Meeting
The board discussed two grant opportunities. The first is a seasonal community grant of $58,946
with an application deadline of August 28th, which Brett Roberts from Berkshire Regional
Planning Commission has offered to help prepare. The second is a potential $20,000 cooperative
grant with another town that Jim Harwood is investigating. Peg reported on the CDC one-stop
grant program, noting that Ian will revise the scope of work and they are awaiting billing
information.
The board scheduled their next meeting for July 20th at 8:30am.
Mary Brazie,
Recording Secretary

Water Commission
June 23, 2026, 9:30am
Attending in person were Chair Mary Brazie, member Judi Goodman and Vice-Chair Lucinda
Vermeulen, Water Operator Nate Stalker, Dan Buttrick from Tighe & Bond. Attending via zoom were
Water Secondary Operator/Clerk Taylor Thompson, Grant Administrator Peg McDonough, Peter
Valinski from Tighe & Bond.
The meeting was audio and video recorded.
The commission approved minutes from the June 4th meeting.
Karner Brook Dam Rehabilitation Options
The Water Commissioners meeting focused on reviewing a report analyzing rehabilitation
alternatives for the Karner Brook Dam. Dan from Tighe & Bond Engineering presented findings from
their site assessment, including geotechnical surveys, underwater inspections of internal chambers,
and analysis of flood risks. The team identified two main alternatives: building a new dam
downstream or repairing the existing structure by relocating electrical controls, installing a
submersible pump, and buttressing the downstream side. The discussion revealed uncertainty about
property ownership boundaries and the need for a survey before proceeding with any construction
project, which could take approximately two and a half years of design and permitting once funded.
The board discussed two dam alternatives for the water treatment facility, with costs of $5.1 million
for replacement and $4.0 million for rehabilitation, not including temporary interconnection or
engineering fees. The group expressed preference for a new dam due to longer lifespan and better
accessibility, though the cost difference is relatively small after accounting for interconnection
expenses. Peg indicated that federal grants through USDA would likely be the primary funding
source, potentially providing around 45% of the total cost, with state funding possible for engineering
and permitting phases. The team agreed to remove specific recommendations from the report and
focus on presenting both options to the town for decision.
The discussion revealed that a previous MVP grant application was not filed due to the fact that this
engineering report was not ready in time.
Water Interconnection Options Discussion
The group discussed two options for water interconnection between Egremont and Great Barrington:
a temporary connection costing approximately $500,000 for 5,400 feet of pipe, and a permanent
connection estimated at $3.5 million. Peter explained that Great Barrington has previously
interconnected with Housatonic Water Works and would likely support a connection with Egremont,
with wholesale rate pricing based on water volume.

Prior Business
Discussion of revised Planning Board Articles at Special Town Meeting June 23rd. PB reviewed emails concerning
slaughterhouses. Email and Maggie’s List concerns include-
 Location of a brick-and-mortar facility and size of such a facility
 Increase in traffic and trailers to the area as it could draw business from other nearby communities.
 Effluent and run-off
 General pollution concerns. PB noted that regulations exist for rendering- (disposing of hides, and unusable
components) this work is outsourced to companies.
 Emotions related to actual slaughtering. Christian S. noted that 90% of what a facility does is cutting, processing,
and packaging.

 Ownership and management changes at Goodnow Farm.

reviewing input from Town Boards, soliciting public feedback through a variety of forums before reaching a
decision.

rural district as opposed to a “no” as it currently stands. Intention of the PB was to support local agriculture.
Planning Board reviewed the opportunity over the past year for the public to educate and offer feedback. Group
discussed an upcoming open virtual forum by Jake Levin to offer accurate information and respond to community
concerns. This meeting will be in advance of the Special Town Meeting and the Board is hopeful the public will avail
themselves of the opportunity.
PB members then reviewed upcoming individual Articles to be presented at the Special Town Meeting. Confirmed
overall goal is to have as many articles pass as possible. Acknowledged that a strategy change may need to occur if
Article 5, which has the scheduled use table, generates public concern and feedback. Group considered whether
pivoting slaughterhouse from special permit back to a “no” will allow other articles to pass.

July 1, 2026
INTRODUCTION AND JURISDICTION
The Egremont Planning Board (the “Board”) held a duly noticed public hearing under M.G.L. c. 40A and the
Egremont Zoning Bylaw. The Board considered Greenagers’ application for an Annual Renewable Special
Permit for a yearly recurring event on the second Friday of August on the Greenagers’ property.
The Planning Board is the Special Permit Granting Authority for the use under §7.3 and §5.2.4 of the Zoning
Bylaw.
A supermajority of Planning Board members was present: Mary McGurn, Chair. John Lanterman, Vice-Chair,
Donna-Bersch Gordon, Eddie Regendahl, and Blake McDonald, Associate Member sitting in for absent member,
Stephan Lyle.
PROJECT DESCRIPTION
Greenagers is an active nonprofit educational organization operating at the Undermountain Road property,
and the annual gala is accessory and supportive of Greenagers’ nonprofit educational mission.
The permit request is for an Annual Special Permit for one recurring annual, ticketed fundraiser, held on the
second Friday of August each year, renewable annually at the Greenagers’ location on Undermountain Rd.
Annual renewal is subject to compliance with the permit conditions.
Special Permit Findings (§7.3)
For each of the following, the Board discussed and agreed the standard was met, then took a
unanimous “yes” position on all 6 conditions:
1. Compliance with Zoning & Intent of Bylaw
o Finding: The proposed annual Greenagers gala complies with the zoning bylaw
and is in harmony with the general intent and purposes.
o Vote: Unanimous YES
2. Public Convenience or Welfare
o Finding: The use is essential or desirable to the public convenience or
welfare at this location (standard language from the bylaw).
o Vote: Unanimous YES
3. No Detriment to Adjacent Uses / Neighborhood Character
o Finding: The event will not be detrimental to adjacent uses or to the
established or planned future character of the neighborhood.
o Vote: Unanimous YES
4. Traffic & Pedestrian Safety
o Finding: The event will not create undue traffic congestion or unduly
impair pedestrian safety.
o Vote: Unanimous YES
5. Municipal Services / Public Health & Safety
o Finding: The event will not overload public water, drainage, sewer, or
other municipal facilities in a way that creates public health, safety, or
welfare hazards.
o Vote: Unanimous YES
6. Other Required Licenses & Permits
o Finding: The applicant has obtained (or will obtain in the ordinary course) all
required variances, licenses, and permits (e.g., one-day liquor license, Board
of Health/caterer approvals, tent permits) prior to the permit decision taking
effect. The Board was satisfied, based on past practice and current
information, that these will be in place.
o Vote: Unanimous YES
ANNUAL SPECIAL PERMIT DETERMINATION (§5.2.4 – COMMUNITY OR FARM EVENT)
The Board also made and agreed on the required determinations for an annual special
permit:
1. Maximum Number of Events per Year
o Finding: Maximum of one (1) event per year under this permit (the annual
fundraising gala only).
o Vote: Unanimous YES
2. Maximum Attendance per Event
o Finding: Maximum of 250 attendees, including guests and vendors/staff
(application cited 200 guests plus up to ~50 additional vendors).
o Vote: Unanimous YES.
3. Approved Location
o Finding: Event location is April Hill / Greenagers property at 62 North
Undermountain Road, South Egremont, in the rural residential district, as
shown on the site plan (tent, prep tent, garden/cocktail area, and field
parking).
o Vote: Unanimous YES.
4. Parking Surface Condition

MEETING OF THE SELECT BOARD
MINUTES
******************************************************************************
Date: June 30, 2026
Time: 10:00 A.M.
Place: Via Zoom Meeting & Town Hall
Egremont
Present at the meeting in person were Select Board Chairwoman Lucinda Vermeulen, Vice
Chairwoman Judi Goodman, Board Member Mary Brazie, Administrative Assistant Mindy
Nilson, Road Superintendent Jim Noe, Danielle Latzman, Donna Bersch Gordon, and Web
Administrator Peg McDonough, Fire Chief Joe Schneider, Ezra Smith, and Joseph Keefner
Present via zoom was Mary McGurn, Joyce Frater, Eileen Vining, Marj Wexler, Bruce Mallory,
Dan Blitzer, and Personnel Director Cara Becker.
The meeting was audio and video recorded.
ACCEPTANCE OF MINUTES:
The minutes of the June 2 and June 16 minutes were accepted with minor edits. The
minutes from the June 23 closed session meeting were accepted as presented.
SCHEDULED ISSUES:
Danielle Latzman and Donna Bersch Gordon, residents of Blunt Rd. and Ridge Rd. came
before the Select Board to discuss pedestrian and traffic safety on their roads. The main
discussion centered on safety concerns raised by residents. They requested traffic safety
improvements including speed feedback signs, enhanced warning signs. Jim Noe, the highway
superintendent, indicated that while signage improvements could be addressed, traffic calming
measures would require traffic studies and coordination with the police department, and the
board committed to working with residents to evaluate practical safety solutions. Jim Noe agreed
to meet with Danielle to discuss next steps in addressing the problem. Cara Becker suggested the
group contact Walk Massachusetts to see if they can help with walkability audits.
Fire Chief Joe Schneider appeared before the Select Board to present two applicants for
the Fire Responder/EMT positions currently open in Egremont. Chief Schneider recommended
both Ezra Smith and Joseph "JD" Keefner, noting that each candidate is highly qualified.
Ezra Smith is currently completing his EMT training and is expected to receive his
certification on August 1. JD Keefner has already completed all required training and holds the
necessary certifications.
Following interviews with both applicants and discussion of starting salaries, the Select
Board unanimously approved the hiring of both candidates. JD Keefner will begin at an annual
salary of $63,000. Ezra Smith will begin at an annual salary of $60,000, with the potential for a
salary increase upon successful completion of his probationary period and receipt of his EMT
certification.
NEW BUSINESS:
The Select Board approved the appointment of Melanie Vicneiri as part-time Council on
Aging Administrative Assistant and accepted the new job description for Peg Muskrat's outreach
coordinator role.
Police Officer Max Kolb’s request to use town property for firearms certification training
has been deferred.
The discussion regarding the Seasonal Community Designation funding has been
deferred.
OLD BUSINESS:
The Select Board as well as the Finance Committee unanimously approved an
interdepartmental transfer of $2,000 from the Assessors-QDS conversion account to the
Computer expenses account to cover computer expenses to the end of the year.
The annual re-appointments/appointments of the Emergency Management has been
deferred.
The discussion surrounding the Web Administration moving forward has been deferred.
The Select Board discussed various grant updates and administrative matters, including a
potential contract with Berkshire Regional Planning Commission for grant administration
services not exceeding $10,000. There will be further discussion at a later date.
GRANTS:
Grant discussion was minimal as Peg McDonough has wrapped most grants up and
closed out those completed.
David Seligman has approved the C-Sip grant for Karner Ridge invasives/Bird habitat. It was
estimated at $7,000 but has come in under that amount at just over $6,000. This grant does have
a 50/50 match.
The Rural Development Fund was completed on 6/30/26.
FY27 MassDOT Community Culvert Grant has been submitted and is pending.
The FY26 Green Communities Grant for Water plant insulation in the amount of $31,276
has a completion date of 6/30/26
The FY26 Drought Resiliency and Water Efficiency Grant for the Water Department

--- MINUTES ---

Date: July 7, 2026
Time: 6:30 PM
Place: via Zoom
Present at the meeting via Zoom were Caleb Chao, Kate Sontag, Emily Eyre and Ronnie Sacco
Committee Chair Kate Sontag called the meeting to order. Minutes from the previous meeting
on March 11, 2026 were approved.
Finances and Donations
• Kate Sontag reported that the current cash balance in the donation box was $149, with
recent payments in the amount of $275 made to Joe Schneider for waste removal
services.
• Kate noted that she calculated a current balance of $812.77 in the FPDP town account;
however, Paul Lisi’s recent accounting report reflected a balance of $1218.84 for the
Dog Park. The Committee agreed to improve communication with Paul to better
understand the accounting system and reconcile current fund balances, with Kate
offering to potentially meet with Paul to clarify the financial figures.
• Emily reported that the Small Dog Group participants raised approximately $3,180
through 14 contributors, which funded the installation of a sally port ($2,880), a dog
waste station ($256.09), and signage ($17 for cement), with $26.91 remaining in the
fund.
• Emily confirmed, after speaking with Mary Brazie, that donors can claim tax deductions
for donations to the French Park system under Section 170.C1 of the Internal Revenue
Code, which could be useful for future fundraising efforts. Several members of the Small
Dog Play group who made significant contributions were able to benefit from this.
• Emily noted that there was no separate “line” for Small Dog Group contributions in the
town accounting report. The Committee agreed that further communication with Paul
was in order to determine whether such donations can be earmarked within the Dog
Park account.
Dog Waste Retrieval and Park Clean-up
• The Committee agreed to increase quarterly payment to Joe Schneider from $250 to
$275 to account for the additional waste station placed in the private play area.
• Kate reported that the Select Board has not had to field any recent complaints about
dog waste not being picked up by dog owners. However, park visitors are still putting
trash in the bins that are exclusively for dog waste.
Small Dog Group
• Emily reported that a safe and fun community space for small dog owners within the
private play area has been successfully created.
• Emily proposed approaching the Select Board about delivering mulch to the private play
area and securing a picnic table to improve the space.
• Ronnie suggested that, given the success of the Small Dog Group and the previous
underutilization of the private play area, the Committee might consider forming
additional specialized play groups. One suggestion presented was the creation of a
playgroup for young dogs under two years old. The Committee agreed to research
potential themes and gather input from park users before implementing any new
programs.
Dog Park Security
• The Committee discussed recent incidents at the Dog Park on July 3. The incident
involved aggressive behavior by multiple dogs and people inside the larger dog park—
and included one dog burrowing under the fence after a small dog in the parking lot.
The police were notified. Fortunately, no one was physically hurt.
• The Committee quickly reached out to Tom Reynolds to request that he reinforce the
fence where dogs could potentially get under it.
• The Committee agreed to hang signs on the entrance gates to both parks which read: “If
your dog exhibits aggressive behavior, leave the park immediately” as well as “enter
at your own risk" to address legal liability concerns.
• Kate confirmed comprehensive communications about the recent incident have been
sent to relevant parties, including copies to members of the Select Board and the
Egremont Police.
Other Business
• The Committee welcomed Emily as the most recently appointed member of the French
Park Dog Park Committee.
The next meeting of FPDP will take place in Fall 2026 via Zoom. Secretary Ronnie Sacco will confirm a
date prior to finalizing the agenda for the meeting.

Transfer Station Working Grodup
July 9, 2026 Minutes approved 9-10-26
The meeting was called to order at 3:30 p.m. at Town Hall with Freddy Friedman, Tara White, Chuck
Loring and Gardiner Morse present, and Marc Trachtenberg absent.
Agenda: 1) Review and approve 6-11-26 minutes; 2) Traffic-path alternative; 3) Permit enforcement
and station access; 4) Communications, signage, battery recycling; 5) Staff training and incident
procedures; 6) Redesign and point-of-sale updates; 7) Other business.
Approval of Minutes
A motion was made and seconded to approve the June 11 meeting minutes. The motion passed.
Traffic-Path Alternative
The group briefly discussed Marc’s alternative redesign concept that would place containers in the
center of the site and route vehicles around them. Freddy said the idea had potential but could
increase attendants’ workload and might require paving. No action was taken.
Permit Renewal and Enforcement
The group reviewed the permit-renewal process. Permits expired June 30, with July serving as a
grace period. Attendants would begin actively checking stickers on August 1. There was some
discussion of whether attendants would start turning people without stickers away in August or
September, but no final decision. Freddy noted problems in the online renewal system involving
missing addresses. Jennifer Greenberg has reportedly fixed this. Gardiner experienced similar
problems and mentioned that several other residents had complained about glitches in the system.
The discussion then turned to misuse of the two-sticker-per-household permit, including stickers
being shared with people outside the permitted household. The group revisited Tara’s suggestion of
adapting Sheffield’s model for identifying households that use private curbside collection, which
could provide a more accurate accounting of who should be paying for transfer-station access. No
change was adopted.
Communications, Signage and Battery Recycling
Gardiner reviewed the performance of the station’s communications channels, noting that clear on-
site signs and direct communication from attendants and volunteers are the most reliable ways to
reach station users. The group agreed that “employees only” signage to keep residents out of the
metal container should be considered. The discussion then moved to making the station’s battery-
recycling program more visible and easier to understand with enhanced signage and potentially a
periodic “battery day,” with a knowledgeable person available to sort batteries and answer
questions. Tara has submitted a grant application for a shed that would provide improved storage
for batteries and light bulbs, and said she expected to hear about the grant sometime between
October and December. To reduce resident information overload, Gardiner proposed a series of
short rotating educational campaigns on priority topics including recycling and Swap Shop use.
Safety Vests
The group discussed buying lightweight reflective vests marked “Attendant” to increase safety and
to help residents identify attendants. Chuck pointed out that on medical calls safety vests have
proven valuable in signaling the wearers’ role. Freddy noted that station vests had been ordered
several years ago but, through a mix-up, had been returned. Gardiner will look into pricing and
production options for new vests.
Staff Training and Incident Procedures
The group revisited the need for a clear accident and incident procedure. Employees and work-off
participants should promptly report even minor injuries because delayed reporting can complicate
insurance claims. The group agreed that all attendants and work-off participants should attend a
dedicated training meeting that would cover accident reporting, fees, recycling and other station
rules, and other areas to ensure that all involved had consistent information.
Redesign, Point-of-Sale System, and Technology
As Marc was not present, there was no substantive redesign or point-of-sale system update. The
group agreed that any system used for municipal operations must be owned or formally controlled
by the town, administered through appropriate town employees or contractors, and compatible
with the town’s financial and information-technology requirements. Tara raised related questions
about ownership and administrative control of the station’s camera and network systems.
Adjournment
With no further business, a motion was made and seconded to adjourn. The motion passed, and the
meeting was adjourned at approximately 4:43 p.m.
Action Items
 Prepare permit-renewal handouts, begin active sticker checks August 1, and confirm the date on
which vehicles without renewed permits will be denied entry. (Freddy, attendants)
 Develop an “employees only” sign for the metal container. (Gardiner)
 Prepare battery-recycling signage and a short educational campaign; revisit a periodic battery
education/sorting day if the storage shed is funded. (Gardiner, Tara)
 Obtain pricing and production options for reflective vests marked for transfer-station
attendants. (Gardiner)
 Draft a written accident and incident reporting procedure for employees, work-off participants,
and members of the public. (Not assigned)
 Coordinate a training meeting for all attendants and work-off participants. (Not assigned)
 Clarify town ownership, administration, and IT-integration requirements for the point-of-sale,
camera, and network systems. (Not assigned)

Egremont Planning Board Minutes
• Meeting date: July 10, 2026
• Location: Zoom
• Chair: Mary McGurn
• Board members present: John Lanterman; Stephen Lyle; Donna Bersch-Gordon; Eddie
Regendahl
• Board members absent: Blake McDonald
• Guests: Eileen Vining
• Call to Order time: 10:00 AM
• Adjournment time: 12:11 PM
• Next meeting date/time: July 22, 2026 at 10:00 AM (Zoom)
Key Outputs with motions and vote results
• Chapter 61A releases: The Board reached consensus, without a formal motion or vote,
that it did not object to the Select Board declining the Town’s right of first refusal for the
McLaughlin parcel and the two Burdsall/Birdsell family properties. Chair McGurn said
she would adapt the written response and send it to the Select Board.
• Fees: The Board reaffirmed the previously discussed three-tier site plan review fees of
$250 minor, $500 standard, and $750 major. It also reached consensus on a special
permit administrative fee of $350 plus actual notice costs; Chair McGurn will determine
how to implement the change. The proposed $100 site-plan-modification fee was held
for further review.
• EOHLC Seasonal Community grant: The Board supported continuing to refine a three-
component proposal centered on activating existing housing tools, Municipal Housing
Trust implementation needs, and site/infrastructure feasibility. Members emphasized
moving quickly toward specific sites and buildable housing opportunities. The proposal
was to be circulated and taken to the Municipal Housing Trust for its July 20 meeting.
• Next priorities: Clean-energy siting/battery storage was identified as time-sensitive;
agritourism, the Historical Commission’s revised demolition-delay bylaw, bicycle
connections, and proactive housing implementation were also identified for follow-up.
Agenda Item Discussion
Form A: None
Chair McGurn reported that there were no Form A applications ready for action. She said Mike Parsons
had not been able to complete an expected filing in time but anticipated receiving one later and asked
the Board to keep that in mind when scheduling the next meeting. No action was taken.
Review and approval of minutes (if applicable): None.
Chapter 61A release: McLaughlin & Burdsall
Mary McGurn explained that the Select Board had asked the Planning Board and Conservation
Commission for comments on three Chapter 61A release matters: one involving McLaughlin and two
involving the Burdsall family. She reported that the Conservation Commission had left the matter to the
Select Board’s discretion and noted that the Select Board has a 120-day period in which to decide
whether to exercise the Town’s right of first refusal or otherwise act.
For the two Burdsall properties, she described one Baldwin Hill property as remaining within the family
and another Baldwin East property, previously used as a long-term rental, as being sold outside the
family. John Lanterman asked questions about the locations and existing houses. The discussion also
noted that the purchase prices were substantial, making municipal acquisition difficult.
For McLaughlin, Mary McGurn said approximately two acres were being separated from a roughly 20-
acre Chapter 61A agricultural property near Creamery Road/Townhouse Road, with approximately 18
acres remaining in agricultural use. The two-acre parcel was described as vacant land intended for a
single-family house, with a price of approximately $225,000. Members discussed whether land released
from Chapter 61A could ever present an opportunity for affordable or attainable housing, and Stephen
Lyle noted that the Municipal Housing Trust and Community Preservation Act (CPA) resources could
potentially help the Town be prepared for future opportunities.
Mary McGurn read proposed response language stating that the Planning Board saw no planning reason
for the Town to acquire the McLaughlin residential parcel and did not object to the Select Board
declining the Town’s right of first refusal, subject to statutory and tax matters being addressed. Members
concurred with the Planning Board’s response to the Select Board.
Fee Update: Site Plan Review tiers & Special Permit
Mary McGurn reviewed the Board’s previously discussed three-tier site plan review fee structure: $250
for minor review, $500 for standard review, and $750 for major review. John Lanterman said the
recommendation appeared reasonable.
Mary McGurn proposed a flat $100 fee for a modification to an approved site plan where abutter notice
would be involved. This led to discussion about who should bear the cost and responsibility for abutter
notification. The Board distinguished site plan review, where its guidelines had voluntarily added abutter
notice for cottage-cluster review, from special permits, where notice requirements are in zoning and the
Planning Board is responsible for the notices.
Members discussed the existing 300-foot abutter radius, the use of first-class mail versus certificate of
mailing, and whether the site plan review guidelines should be amended so the applicant is responsible
for obtaining the abutter list and paying the associated notice costs. Members did not want to eliminate
abutter notice. Discussion will continue at the next scheduled Planning Board meeting. The $100
modification fee was therefore held rather than adopted.
For special permits, Mary McGurn explained that the current $500 fee no longer covers the Planning
Board’s costs, especially two consecutive weeks of legal notices in the Berkshire Eagle, plus mailed
notices to abutters and abutting towns. The Board discussed charging a lower administrative fee plus the
actual notice costs. Members expressed consensus for a $350 administrative fee plus actual notice costs.
Mary McGurn will determine how the special permit fee change is to be implemented and where the fee
schedule should be published or incorporated.
CPC Committee request/timeline: Stephen Lyle
Stephen Lyle reported on Community Preservation Committee (CPC) work. He said the committee was
developing an application template for boards and individuals to propose uses of Community
Preservation Act funds and that he had been assigned to prepare a rough first draft of the overall plan.
The CPC was also developing a timetable so recommendations could move through the Select Board and
ultimately Town Meeting.
Stephen said boards would be solicited before the general public and that there would be a public
hearing. Donna Bersch-Gordon asked whether money could be placed automatically into the Municipal

approval, though the CPC could make recommendations.

infrastructure, particularly connections involving South Egremont Village, North Egremont Village, Great
Barrington, and Route 23, citing safety, economic-development, and village-activity benefits. Stephen
supported the concept and referenced the economic value of trail systems. Mary McGurn said the
Planning Board should develop several project ideas fitting the CPC categories and that she would share
the CPC’s formal request when received.

period would open August 3 and close August 28. Eligible activities included housing planning,
zoning/bylaw work, design and engineering, affordable or attainable housing work, trust support, and

Housing Trust Board
July 20, 2026, 8:30am
Present in the meeting room were Chairman Richard Stanley, Vice-Chairman Doug Mishkin, and
members Judi Goodman and Evan Hardcastle. Also present at Town Hall were Brett Roberts of
Berkshire Regional Planning Commission and John Lanterman. Present via Zoom were Lucinda
Vermeulen, Rebecca Heidgard, Mary McGurn, and Stephen Lyle.
The meeting was video and audio recorded.
Minutes of the June 23 and June 29 meetings were accepted with minor edits.
Egremont Housing Grant Discussion
The Board discussed the $58,000 seasonal communities funding from EOHLC with Brett Roberts
from Berkshire Regional Planning Commission who explained the three potential uses for the funds:
planning and zoning, local actions for housing development, and public horizontal infrastructure
projects. As Egremont’s zoning is compliant, Brett recommended not focusing on that area. The
board discussed using the funds for adding water and sewer infrastructure to support additional
housing units, with estimated costs ranging from $20,000 to $40,000. It was agreed to have Brett
provide cost estimates and information about a housing audit company by the end of the week, with
a follow-up meeting scheduled for August 4th at 9:30 AM (later changed to August 3 at 8:30am) to
review the proposal before the August 28th grant deadline.
Brett clarified that a year-round housing trust is not necessary to accept the funds, but is still trying to
get clarity if the town could designate its current housing trust to serve the purposes for this grant
program. The funds received will be earmarked for specific projects, not put in the town’s general
fund. There is a 250% AMI limitation if the Town gives the funds to the CDC. Brett clarified that
the funds for public horizontal infrastructure projects includes roads, sewer, water, etc. There seems
to be no link to the funds and an affordable housing project.
Short-Term Rental Monitoring Services
The failed short-term rental bylaw was also discussed. The meeting focused on discussing short-
term rental monitoring services, with participants exploring options for hiring contractors to provide
necessary statistics. The group noted that Granicus had approached them as a potential service
provider, and they discussed the possibility of hiring them based on positive feedback from other
towns who found them to be more cost-effective with better results than previous providers. As well
the Donohue Institute could be helpful. Ultimately, a majority of the Board agreed to recommend
that the Select Board appoint an adhoc working group to address the issue separately from the
Housing Trust.
Housing Project:
There are two potential buyers working through the process and more being sought. CDC is
working on creating an entry for the project so that it doesn’t look like an affordable housing project.
More detail to be presented at the next meeting. Stephen Lyle asked about a master plan for the 6
acre town lot that is being developed for housing. There is an older plan that the CDC will consider
in making a plan for future development.
Community Preservation Act
The Board also reviewed plans for Community Preservation Act (CPA) funding, discussing potential
uses including down payment assistance, rental assistance, and infrastructure improvements for
affordable housing projects. It was agreed to gather more information about existing programs and
constraints before making specific funding requests to the CPA committee, and to determine if there
are down payment assistance and rental assistance program’s available to Egremont residents that
the CPA could support with funds. It was suggested that two members connect separately to
develop proposals for CPA funding uses.
The housing trust fund balance is very low with a balance of $100, while the separate short-term
rental impact fee balance is $323.
The next meeting date was scheduled for Monday, August 3rd at 8:30 AM.
These minutes are taken from Zoom AI notes and a review of the recording of the meeting.

Recording Secretary

Discuss Town Hall Renovations—direction/next steps
Before EDM submits a final proposal to the Town for architectural services, the Committee
reviewed and refined the scope of the work. There was a discussion on whether all work should
start from scratch or if the most recent schematics (produced by EDM in 2021) could be used as
a jumping off point. The committee reviewed the schematic which depicts an addition to house
an elevator and new staircase to provide accessibility to the upper floor. There was a discussion
on alternative options such as moving the building and potentially siting it to allow the upper
story to be at ground level, and/or using just one floor of the building and avoiding the need for
an elevator. After discussion, all present agreed that the proposed Town Hall renovation should
include use of both the upper and lower floors. Some felt the building should remain in its
current location. The Committee also agreed that an elevator was preferred over a lift. The
Committee asked EDM to provide a schematic with the elevator and new staircase inside the
existing building with no addition as an alternative option to the addition.

work.

the programming needs. EDM will bring the program to the Committee for review. It will be
reviewed by the Select Board. The public will be notified and invited to comment. The
