Housing Trust Board
August 3, 2026, 8:30am
Present at Town Hall were the Trust Board members Richard Stanley, Doug Mishkin, Mary Brazie,
Judi Goodman and Evan Hardcastle. Present via zoom where Brett Roberts (BRPC), Mary McGurn,
Chris Mollomo and arriving later Rebecca Heidegard.
The meeting was audio and visually recorded.
Housing Trust Minutes Correction Meeting
Doug raised concerns about the accuracy of the minutes from the July 20th meeting regarding the
Housing Trust Board's position on short-term rental monitoring services. He clarified that while a
majority of the board may have agreed to recommend that the Select Board form an ad hoc working
group, he personally did not support this recommendation. The motion to approve the minutes was
amended to reflect "a majority of the board" instead of the original wording, and the corrected
minutes were approved.
Seasonal Communities Grant Application Update
Brett provided an update on a grant application for housing infrastructure, explaining that the
application opens today at noon and is due August 28th. He is working with four South County towns
(including Egremont) and will send a proposal outlining two potential uses: expanded water and
wastewater systems and planning work related to housing studies. Brett indicated he would provide
the application materials by tomorrow afternoon, after which the town would need to review and
potentially schedule a meeting to discuss next steps.
Infrastructure Funding Discussion Meeting
The group discussed infrastructure funding for the town project, with Evan expressing concerns
about spending money on septic and water systems before site planning is complete. Brett clarified
that infrastructure funds can be used for pre-construction engineering work, which was seen as a
more sensible approach. The discussion also covered plans for a gate and fence, with Mary noting
that these were initially supposed to be part of a rural development grant but were left out, and that
Jim Harwood is working with Jim Noe to determine the exact location and costs.
Land Gift Process Discussion
Richard updated the board on a land gift situation where clarification was needed about whether to
give the land to CDC or the town, with Mary indicating it needs to go to town meeting ifthe gift is to
he Town.
Housing Project marketing
The board discussed challenges with the 80% AMI unit lottery process, which is estimated to cost
$15,000 through a third-party agency, with participants expressing concern about this being an
excessive expense for the project. The group discussed potential next steps including reaching out
to Lee Davis and the Executive Office of Housing to address the onerous certification requirements
for the lottery process. Meanwhile CDC is looking to work with another agency, such as Berkshire
Housing, for the lottery process.
Community Preservation Funds
The meeting focused on discussing investment strategies for housing projects and CPA funding
allocation. Evan raised concerns about investing additional funds in the current site without seeing
results, suggesting they should consult with CDC president Jim Harwood about further investment
decisions. The group debated how to present their CPA funding request, with consensus to focus
primarily on the housing development project while potentially allocating some funds for rental
assistance through agencies such as Construct.
Affordable Housing Trust exemption program
Mary reported that she sent out a reminder to the former application for the Affordable Housing Tax
Exemption program to reapply, as well as an email on the town’s notices list to all tax payers who
might qualify.
The Board scheduled a follow-up meeting for August 11th at 9 AM to review the seasonal
communities application for the with Brett Roberts and will invite Jim Hardwood to give an update on
the housing site project and marketing of the units.
Mary Brazie,
Recording Secretary

New Marlborough Agricultural Commission Meeting Minutes for Tuesday Aug 4th, 2026
18:30-19:21
Quick recap
The Town of New Marlborough Agricultural Commission held their first meeting to discuss goals
and next steps for reorganizing the group. The commission elected Jake Levin as chair and
Mike Mudridge as vice chair. Key discussion points included reaching out to Sarah Gardner
from MDAR for technical assistance on agricultural commission operations and land acquisition,
conducting a local agricultural census to better understand the diversity of farming operations in
the Town of New Marlborough, and planning public information meetings to address
misinformation about agricultural activities. The group discussed the need to educate Town of
New Marlborough residents about what constitutes farming and agricultural operations, with
particular focus on addressing concerns about meat processing and slaughterhouses. They also
explored the possibility of holding special topic meetings with agricultural experts and inviting all
farmers in the Town of New Marlborough to participate in a census to demonstrate the breadth
and variety of agricultural operations. The commission agreed to meet monthly at 6:30 PM on
the first Tuesday of each month, starting September 1st, with Jake handling meeting
coordination and minutes through Mari.
Next steps
Town of New Marlborough
● Reach out to Sarah Gardner to coordinate her attendance at the next meeting for technical
assistance.
● Contact Mari to check if the first Tuesday of the month at 6:30 PM works for regular
meetings and to inquire if Jennifer can take the meeting minutes.
● Send out the agenda for the next meeting and ensure it is posted publicly 48 hours in
advance.
● Start working on a draft for a farmer census/survey to be discussed at the next meeting.
● Reach out to Bob Kilmer as a fallback speaker for the next meeting if Sarah Gardner is
unavailable.
● Begin compiling a list of local and regional subject matter experts (SMEs) for future
reference.
● Plan a special meeting to invite all farmers in the town to introduce themselves and discuss
their operations.
● Advertise the next meeting (September 1st) on Maggie's List, Five Village News, and post
notices in the library and Southfield Post Office.
Summary
Board Meeting Leadership Election
The meeting began with introductions of board members, including Jake Levin, Christian
Stovall, Tom Brazie, Mike Mudridge, and Matt Ferrara. The group discussed scheduling, noting
that planning board meetings currently occur on the second and fourth Tuesdays at 6 or 6:30
PM, though this schedule is under review. The conversation ended with discussions about
electing a chair and vice chair, with Jake Levin volunteering to serve as chair.
Ag Commission Officer Elections
The meeting focused on electing officers for the Ag Commission, with Jake Levin elected as
chair and Mike nominated as vice chair. The group discussed seeking technical assistance from
Sarah Gardner, a MDAR technician who provides free support to ag commissions, particularly
regarding land acquisition capabilities and standard bylaws. The discussion included insights
about other active Berkshire County ag commissions, particularly highlighting Sheffield's
commission and resources like Bob Kilmer and Paul Turner.
Agricultural Information and Expert Resources
The discussion focused on addressing misinformation and lack of accurate information about
agriculture in Town of New Marlborough meetings, particularly regarding slaughterhouses and
farming operations. The participants agreed on the need to create a public list of local
agricultural experts and resources to help balance information during Town of New Marlborough
discussions. They also discussed conducting a census of active agricultural operations in the
Town of New Marlborough to better understand the diversity of farming practices and
relationships to land, moving beyond the typical few individuals who dominate Town of New
Marlborough meetings.
New Marlborough Agricultural Challenges
The discussion focused on agricultural challenges in the Town of New Marlborough, particularly
regarding opposition to farming and meat processing operations. Participants discussed the
need to educate residents about agricultural practices and address misinformation about
environmental impacts, with one speaker emphasizing that small farms pose minimal risk to
groundwater. The group explored the possibility of inviting agricultural speakers to future
meetings and considered developing a strategic vision for agriculture in the Town of New
Marlborough, though they noted challenges in getting residents to attend regular meetings.
New Marlborough Agricultural Meeting Planning
The discussion focused on planning an agricultural meeting in the Town of New Marlborough.
TBW advised that to ensure good attendance, the meeting should be advertised as having a
specific speaker and agenda, rather than just an informational session. The group agreed to
follow public meeting laws by posting publicly and emailing Maggie's list about the meeting.
They discussed the format, which would include introductions of the new Agricultural
Commission members, a presentation by a speaker, and an opportunity for public questions.
The conversation ended with a discussion about defining what constitutes a farm and the variety
of farming operations in the area.
Agricultural Commission Meeting Planning
The agricultural commission discussed organizing farmer outreach efforts and establishing
meeting procedures. They agreed to conduct a monthly meeting starting September 1st at 6:30
PM, with plans to invite all farmers in the Town of New Marlborough to participate in a census
and special topic meeting. The group also addressed conflict of interest concerns, deciding that
representing all farmers rather than individual interests would not constitute a conflict, and
established guidelines for communication through the chair to ensure transparency in decision-
making processes.

Egremont Board of Health
Thursday, August 6, 2026, 10:30 am
In Attendance: Charles Ogden
Also Present: Jazu Stine, Berkshire County Health Alliance Field Agent, Mike Parson, Kelly,
Granger & Parsons, Todd Wilkinson, Wilkinson Excavating
Recording: Juliette Haas, Director
1) BOH Chairman Charles Ogden called the meeting to order at 10:35 am. Introductions were
made for all present, either in person or on Zoom. Juliette Haas, Associate Member, was
called upon for this meeting to act as a voting member, as the regular members were not
present. Approval of the minutes from the July 9, 2026 meeting was tabled until a quorum of
committee members is present.
2) Food Permit Renewal Changes Alliance Health Agent Jazu Stine proposed a change in
permit fees for food establishments based on FDA risk levels, rather than the “a la carte” fee
schedule currently in place. Jazu stated that this change would make food permitting more
efficient and would work in conjunction with the Food Code, based on the level of risk for the
type of food being served. The proposal would change the current fees in Egremont food
establishments as
follows:
Current Fee Proposed Fee
North Egremont Store $110 $210
Harmony Market $120 $210
Mom’s $ 75 $200
The Mill $150 $300
Buttonball Inn $225 $300
The Cliff House $100 $300
The Prospect/Snack Shack $ 75 $150
Hilltown Hot Pies $150 $300
Catamount Lodge $200 $300
Catamount Cafeteria $200 $200
Residential Kitchens $75 $150
Chairman Ogden agreed with making the change based on Jazu’s proposal but asked that it
be put on the agenda for the next meeting when the other board members are present.
3) Harmony Market/Main Street Director Haas spoke to Tammy in person. The handwashing
sink at the gelato store is waiting for the delivery of the sink. Director Haas also spoke to
Tammy about the portable toilet that has been in place outside the gelato store for the past
few weeks. The portable toilet was located less than 3 feet from ledge to Karner Brook and is
in an Area of Critical Environmental Concern (ACEC). Tammy stated to Director Haas that
she will have the portable toilet removed.
4) 138 Hillsdale Road/Sheldon A Title 5 inspection was recently performed on the 15-year-old
septic system at this location by Jennifer Sweet of Berkshire Pittsfield Septic and witnessed
by James Massey of the Alliance. Due to what was thought to be solids in the dbox and the
beginning of the lines, the system failed. The homeowner then contacted Wilkinson
Excavating and Kelly, Granger, & Parsons to further inspect. Both Todd Wilkinson and Mike
Parsons agreed the system should not have been deemed a failure. They felt the system was
not inspected fully, and the inspector did not open the inspection port on the lines. The dbox
was not filled with solids from the tank, only soil from the surrounding area due to a crushed
outlet on the tank, and all the septic lines were clean and dry. Based on the evidence
presented by Mr. Wilkinson and Mr. Parsons, the Board agreed to rescind the results of the
Title 5 inspection performed by Jennifer Sweet. Director Haas will contact Ms. Sweet and ask
for another inspection and report. Todd Wilkinson offered to provide a new report if Ms.
Sweet is not agreeable to performing another inspection. The system needs a new outlet on
the tank and a new dbox. The Wilkinson Title 5 report will either be a Pass if those repairs are
made, or a Conditional Pass while the repairs are waiting to be made.
5) Installation of Town Hall PFAS Treatment Unit The deadline for quotes has expired. B&T
Well & Pump was the only firm that submitted an estimate. Chairman Ogden made a motion
to recommend hiring B&T Well & Pump to the Select Board. Vote taken 2-0. In the event the
grant funds don’t completely cover the installation costs, the remaining funds will be taken
from the BOH expense budget.
6) Microplastics Survey Director Haas presented a draft email to be sent to the town’s email
list on the results of the survey with microplastic reduction tips. The draft was approved and
will be posted in the next few days.
7) Recent Field Work
10 Baldwin Hill South/Title 5/Juliette/failed due to groundwater
10 Baldwin Hill South/Repair Perc/Alliance
18 Hilltop Rd/Alliance/Title 5/Conditional Pass – needs new dbox
8) Meeting adjourned at 11:28 am. The next meeting is scheduled for August 20th.
Approved 8/20/2026
JHaas

Housing Trust Board
August 11, 2026, 9:00am
Present at Town Hall were the Trust Board members Richard Stanley, Doug Mishkin, Mary Brazie,
Judi Goodman and Evan Hardcastle and arriving later Jim Harwood(CDC). Present via zoom where
Brett Roberts (BRPC), and Mary McGurn.
The meeting was audio and visually recorded.
The minutes of the August 3 meeting were accepted as edited.
Seasonal Communities Grant Application
Brett reported receiving guidance to proceed with a seasonal communities grant application for both
housing analysis/technical assistance ($15,000-20,000) and septic and water work at the Town Hall
site, with total funding of $60,687 available until June 30th, 2027. The board agreed to modify the
application to allow flexibility in using funds either for septic/water work on town-owned property or
technical assistance, with Brett confirming this approach would be acceptable to the grant
administrators.
Housing Development Project Planning
The group discussed plans for possible expansion of the workforce housing development project on
town land. The need for a build-out plan from Jim Scalise is essential, including consideration of
additional gifted land, with engineering costs estimated at around $25,000. Jim Harwood explained
difficulties that the CDC has encountered with the rental lottery. There was discussion over revoking
the Chapter 40B permit, building under the cottage cluster zoning, and/or subdividing the property to
avoid issues with future expansion. Mary McGurn explained the cottage cluster zoning requirements,
which allow for four market rate units on an acre with specific square footage options including tiny
homes, a 1,200 square foot cottage, and a 2,000 square foot duplex. Waivers are available through
the site plan review process for square footage variances rather than requiring a special permit.
The group discussed progress on a the town housing development project; foundations are in,
trenching for utilities is underway, framing for the bottom floors will begin next week and the box for
the top floors will arrive the first week of September. The target date for completion is the end of
October. A ribbon cutting ceremony may take place the week of September 15. Marketing has
garnered a large interest, though no one has begun the application process which should start when
construction is complete.
The next meeting will be September 10 at 8:00 am.

Egremont
Present at the meeting in person were Select Board Chairwoman Lucinda Vermeulen, Vice
Chairwoman Judith Goodman, Board member Mary Brazie, and Administrative Assistant Mindy
Nilson.
Present via zoom was Mary McGurn, and Personnel Director Cara Becker.
The meeting was audio and video recorded.
BUSINESS:
The Select Board unanimously approved a temporary permit for a non-conforming sign at
Buttonball Barn to be displayed from August 7, 2026 to October 4, 2026.
Personnel Director Cara Becker presented a draft contract for the web administration
position, outlining key responsibilities including website maintenance and error corrections. Cara
noted that while the contract specifies main duties, the Select Board retains the right to assign
special projects as needed.
The Board reviewed and approved the contract drafted by the Personnel Director, with
minor formatting changes. The Personnel Director suggested adding a requirement for the web
administration to use the town email instead of personal email, which the Select Board agreed
should be included in writing. Mary Brazie provided additional feedback, noting that the contract
title should change from "Website Administrator" to "Website Administration” and suggested
language to clarify that the contractor is not an employee but a vendor performing web
administration services for the town. Mary Brazie also reiterated the need for a W-9 to be
submitted prior to any work being performed. The Web Administration Contractor will submit an
invoice bi-weekly for hours worked as well as a detailed outline of work performed.
The Board discussed revisions to a web administration contract, focussing on language
around vendor coordination and content approval processes. They agreed to add the wording
from "Civic Plus" to "other service providers" to ensure flexibility for future platforms, and
established a process where content for promotional materials will be drafted by the Office
Administrator, Administrative Assistant or Office Clerk and reviewed before posting.
Mary McGurn emphasized the need to carefully assess the conditions before deciding if
she could proceed with the contract. The Board understood and expressed hope that Mary would
find the updated terms workable, noting it was more aligned with the Select Board's preferences.
Mary McGurn outlined her approach to evaluating the proposal based on the best interests of
both the website and her professional needs, promising a quick decision.
The Select Board put forth a motion to pay Mary McGurn for the week ending August 15,
2026 for hours worked at the rate of $45.00 per hour on the Town’s payroll. Mary Brazie voted
Aye, Judi Goodman voted Aye, and Lucinda Vermeulen voted nay. After further discussion Mary
Brazie withdrew her original vote and Judi Goodman withdrew her second and vote as well. The
Board voted a second time to pay Mary McGurn on the Town’s payroll for this week only at the
rate of $64.23. This was a unanimous vote among all member’s of the Select Board.

Tara B. White called the meeting to order at 6:00pm.
Pledge of Allegiance and Moment of Silence for Veterans
The Pledge of Allegiance was recited and a moment of silence for Veterans was held.
Review and take action on State Preservation Restriction—New Marlborough Village Cemetery (Old
Center Cemetery)
John Schreiber reminded the Board that the Historical Society received a state grant to restore gravestones
in the New Marlborough Village Cemetery aka the Old Center Cemetery in New Marlborough. The
Historical Society was able to raise $20,000 in donations and a $20,000 match was given by the state
grant. With those funds, 56 historic stones have been repaired and restored. A requirement for state
reimbursement is that a preservation restriction is signed, notarized and registered with the Registry of
Deeds. The restriction recognizes the historic significance of the cemetery and prohibits any alterations to
the premises. There is a provision that allows the plots in the front section and the rear section of the
cemetery to be used. It was noted that the document refers to a cemetery on Route 57 because the
original paperwork identifies the cemetery at that location. The cemetery’s present day location is
Hillingdon Road.
Maggie made a motion, Bill seconded, and it was so voted for Tara White to sign the Preservation
Restriction agreement between the Commonwealth of Massachusetts (by and through the
Massachusetts Historical Commission) and the Town of New Marlborough to restrict alterations at
the New Marlborough Village Cemetery.
1

Bill West Aye

The Select Board decided to address this agenda item next.
Review and sign off on Property Tax Senior Work-Off Program hours
Pru Spaulding provided a report on the Senior Work-off Tax Abatement program. In FY26, seniors
worked a total of 617 hours. With this program, seniors can earn $15.00 per hour up to $2,000 annually to
reduce their Real Estate taxes. She said the New Marlborough Farmer’s Market has improved under the
direction of Barbara Flach. Pru said she is proud of the improvements made to local programs for seniors.
Maggie made a motion, Bill seconded, and it was so voted to authorize Tara White to sign off on the
Property Tax Senior Work-Off Program totaling 617 hours of work.
Tara B. White Aye
Bill West Aye
Maggie Arian Aye
Discuss and vote on Amendment to Collective Bargaining Agreement with Highway Union
Mari Enoch explained that the Highway Union questioned the method in which the FY 27 Highway
Union rates were calculated. The rates should not be calculated by increasing the previous year’s
wage by 7% but, but should be calculated sequentially (3% and then 4%) which is actually an
increase of 7.12%. Mari asked the Select Board to sign an amendment that increases pay rates for
Highway employees by .03 and .04 cents an hour to take into account the recalculation. Because the
previous rates were accepted by their Union Representative, but the Select Board has required each Union
member to sign the addendum to the agreement.
Tara made a motion, Bill seconded, and it was so voted to amend the Collective Bargaining
Agreement with a Memorandum of Understanding between the Town of New Marlborough and the
United Public Service Employees Highway Union, and adjust the FY 2027 rates.
Tara B. White Aye
Bill West Aye
Maggie Arian Aye
Discuss Town Hall Program draft for Town Hall renovation
The Board reviewed the Town Hall program as part of the Town Hall Project Renovation. The
documents listed the number and sizes of offices, bathrooms, meeting spaces etc. and presented the
information in both written and schematic form. The program assumes offices, a board meeting room,
and one bathroom upstairs with community space, two bathroom, break/small kitchen, and storage
downstairs. There will also be an elevator and staircase. Mari asked the Board to provide feedback on
the program, as once the program is agreed upon, the next step is to see if the program will fit inside the
existing town hall building. Mari reminded the Board that the Design Review Committee will meet
tomorrow August 17th to discuss the program but the Select Board has final say. The Select Board was in
agreement with the program as presented.

Egremont
Present at the meeting in person were Select Board Chairwoman Lucinda Vermeulen, Vice
Chairwoman Judith Goodman, Board member Mary Brazie, Administrative Assistant Mindy
Nilson, Fred Gordon, Julia Rasch, Bruce Mallory, Corinne Hayes, Board of Health Director
Juliette Haas, co-chair of the Historical Commission Beth Wood, and Ulla Dannebom.
Present via zoom was Mary McGurn, Personnel Director Cara Becker, and Molly Cliff.
The meeting was audio and video recorded.
MINUTES:
The minutes from August 3, 2026 were approved with minor edits. The minutes from
August 12, 2026 were deferred to the next meeting pending several corrections.
SCHEDULED ISSUES:
The interview and possible appointment of Alexander Scarbro as an on- call firefighter
has been deferred until a later date.
Molly Cliff from the Egremont Land Trust provided an update on the invasive plant
removal pilot project at French Park, where Greenagers has been removing burning bush without
the use of chemicals. Elia with Greenagers recommended conducting GIS mapping to determine
the extent and distribution of invasive plants across the park before proceeding with further
removal efforts. The team plans to reassess the regrowth in September before making decisions
about next steps, as burning bush control requires long-term, specific planning due to its
seven-year life cycle.
NEW BUSINESS:
The Select Board unanimously approved the appointment of Bruce Mallory as an
alternate to the Zoning Board of Appeals.
Board of Health Director Juliette Haas spoke about a recent request for quotes to install a
PFAS treatment unit for the well serving the Town Hall and Police Department. The project is
funded by the 2024 Mass DEP Emerging Contaminants in small communities. The grant was
awarded in the amount of $38,000. The request for quotes was sent to 5 area plumbing
contractors and 1 firm bid was received from B&T Pump and Well Service, Inc. Of
Lanesborough Ma, in the amount of $28,035.50. The Board spoke about the issues surrounding
the fact that the water will be turned off for 2 days while the work is being performed. This
means that all of Town Hall as well as the Police Department will be without water or restrooms
for most, if not all, day. Several suggestions were made on how to remedy this situation but no
definitive solution was agreed upon. Judith Goodman suggested asking Legal counsel to review
the contract given by B&T Pump and Well Services Inc. The Select Board approved the work
pending Legal Counsel’s acceptance of the contract.
The Board unanimously approved the appointment of Bill Turner as assistant constable
for both the September 1st and November 3rd elections.
The Board accepted with regret and many thanks the resignation of Juliette Haas from the
Green Committee.
Beth Wood and Ulla Dannebom of the Historical Commission came before the Select
Board to discuss plans for a winter open house at the Historical Archives. The goal of the event is
to draw more community members, particularly younger residents, to the Archives and introduce
them to the resources and history available there.
They shared several ideas for the event and welcomed suggestions from the Select Board on
ways to make it engaging and successful. The Select Board gave its approval for the event and
looks forward to hearing more as plans continue to develop.
The Select Board addressed traffic safety concerns in South Village, where multiple
accidents including a death have occurred since Main Street reconstruction, and decided to draft
two letters: one to MassDOT about safety issues requiring Select Board approval and another to
Mike Fabiano about maintenance concerns including tree branches blocking signs as well as
cutting the grass between the sidewalks and the road.
OLD BUSINESS:
The Select Board unanimously approved a new policy prohibiting pets in the workplace.
Mary Brazie will send an email notifying all employees of the new policy, and signs will be
posted in each Town building.
The Select Board approved an interdepartmental transfer from the Transfer Station
Alternate to the Transfer Station Expenses in the amount of $510. This amount is to cover the
purchase of transfer station stickers.
The Select Board unanimously approved the Web Administration contract. Mary McGurn
requested until Monday, August 24th to review the contract, and a follow-up meeting was
scheduled for August 24th at 9:30 AM.

The Board discussed an update on the Blunt Road Culvert Construction project, which

All other grants have been submitted and are pending.

Present at the meeting in person were Select Board Chairwoman Lucinda Vermeulen, Vice
Chairwoman Judith Goodman, Board member Mary Brazie, Administrative Assistant Mindy
Nilson, and Will Brinker.
Present via zoom was Mary McGurn, Fred Gordon, Donna Bersh-Gordon, and Rolfe Tessem.
The meeting was audio and video recorded.
BUSINESS:
The Select Board discussed the web administration contract with Mary McGurn, Who’s
status has changed from employee to contractor. Mary McGurn raised concerns about the
contract's scope and oversight. The board expressed a desire to seek legal opinion from Jeremia
regarding the contractor versus employee classification. Personnel Director Cara Becker sent an
email noting concerns about Mary McGurn's current role in website management and requested
that work stop until contract agreement is reached.
Rolfe Tessem explained the town's history with the website, noting that after a
comprehensive evaluation process in 2020, they selected Civic Plus as their provider and trained
4 town officials on the system. Mr. Tessem stressed his support for this as an employee website
as an important position, similar to the Town infrastructure.
The discussion highlighted ongoing concerns about the web administrator's role, including
questions about accountability and the need to determine proper direction and oversight of the
position.
Fred Gordon expressed concerns about the significant reduction in the web administrator
compensation, questioning whether the role's responsibilities had decreased or if the previous
compensation was excessive. He spoke of the risks of involving more volunteers in website
management, noting potential data integrity issues and security concerns.
Donna Berch-Gordon raised concerns about the challenges of managing the town website
as a volunteer, highlighting the complexity and potential legal risks involved. She emphasized
the need for a user-friendly system, especially for town employees and volunteers. Mary Brazie
pointed out that the proposed compensation for the web administrator was based on a part-time
role and that a more reasonable rate was suggested.
The Select Board agreed to seek a legal opinion from Jeremia regarding whether Mary
McGurn should be classified as an employee or independent contractor. The Select Board voted
on whether Mary McGurn should stop billing for additional work until this classification is
determined, Judith Goodman made the motion and voted aye, Mary Brazie seconded the motion
and voted aye, while Select Board Chairwoman Lucinda Vermeulen voted nay.

TOWN OF EGREMONT, MASSACHUSETTS
MEETING OF THE SELECT BOARD
MINUTES
******************************************************************************
Date: August 31, 2026
Time: 10:00 A.M.
Place: Via Zoom Meeting & Town Hall
Egremont
Present at the meeting in person were Select Board Chairwoman Lucinda Vermeulen, Vice
Chairwoman Judith Goodman, Board member Mary Brazie, Administrative Assistant Mindy
Nilson, Town Clerk Juliette Haas, Julie Burdsall, Brooke Adams, Emily Eyre, Fire Chief Joe
Schneider, Andrew Stone, and his partner Sheila.
Present via zoom were Mary McGurn, and Personnel Director Cara Becker, Alex Scarbro,
Jonathan Schaefer, William Martin, Emily Garrett, Marj Wexler, and Julie Buyon.
The meeting was audio and video recorded.
MINUTES:
The minutes from August 12, August 18 and August 24 have been deferred to the next
meeting.
HEARING:
The Select Board approved the change of ownership interest, change of officers and
change of manager for Catamount Ski Resort pending ABCC approval.
SCHEDULED ISSUES:
The Select Board unanimously approved the appointment of Alexander Scarbro as an on-
call firefighter member.
The conversation with John Wosczyna has been deferred to a later date.
NEW BUSINESS:
The Select Board unanimously approved the appointment of Brooke Adams to the Green
Committee.
Andrew Stone came before the Select Board to discuss placing a bench and plaque at the
dog park in honor of his mother, Florence Browner. Lucinda explained that four benches are
being donated to the Dog Park and suggested that one of those benches could
potentially be used for this purpose. The Select Board will reach out to the COA regarding the
installation of the plaque. Lucinda also asked if Andrew would consider making a donation to the
dog park fund. Andrew agreed to do so.
Resident Julie Buyon addressed the Select Board via Zoom regarding parking concerns at
Hilltown Hot Pies on Blunt Road. She expressed concern about the limited road space and the
number of vehicles being parked along both sides of Blunt Road.
The Town will draft a letter to the owner of Hilltown Hot Pies inviting him to attend a
September meeting to discuss the parking situation and work toward a solution.
The Select Board unanimously approved the appointment of Julie Burdsall as an election
worker.
The Board discussed establishing a screening committee for town hall key positions
including Board of Health, Town Clerk, Treasurer, and Office Administrator. They agreed on a
committee composition with a Select Board member (Lucinda), Cara Becker, Personnel Director,
Laura Allen, Administrative Assistant Mindy Nilson and the current position holder. Mindy will
reach out to Laura inviting her to participate in this committee.
The Great Barrington Transportation Restructuring Proposal has been postponed to a later
date.
Mary McGurn's resignation as Deputy Emergency Management Director was accepted.
The Select Board discussed vandalism at French Park and agreed to revisit the installation
of cameras and post signs to deter future incidents.
OLD BUSINESS:
After some discussion, the Select Board voted 2 aye, 1 abstaining to keep the Web
Administration as an employee position at $48 per hour with no minimum hours but a maximum
of 12 hours per week, not exceeding the remaining budget of $26,417.16 by June 30th. The board
also agreed to remove requirements for training committee heads on Civic Plus and decided that
content should come from the Select Board rather than the web administration creating it
independently.
GRANTS:
All grants are currently in good standing or pending. No updates at this time.

Design Review Committee
September 1, 2026 4:00 p.m.

Barbara Marchione
Mark Carson

Others Present: Dan Pallotta, Project Manager
Tim Widman, EDM
Meaghan Pallotta
Tara White
Chuck Loring called the meeting to order at 4:01 pm. Tim Widman was granted permission to
record the meeting.
Discuss Town Hall Renovations with Project Manager and Architect
Tim Widman presented some draft layout options of the proposed renovations. The basement
options illustrated 1) keeping the bathrooms in the same area they are now with a multipurpose
space (1,100 sf) which means one has to walk through the multipurpose space to access the
bathrooms and 2) moving the bathrooms up toward the main entrance of the building and
moving the multipurpose room (1,000 sf) to the back. The second option will require more
renovation and reconfiguration while the first option uses more of the existing configuration.
The committee seemed to prefer the second option at this time.
Tim spoke to the desire to preserve the upstairs tall windows. He showed illustrations of
different type of ceiling drops to maintain the look of the windows from the outside.
Alternatively, if the office space was pulled away from the exterior wall, the windows can
remain as they are and natural light can be pulled into interior offices. He presented options and
renderings showing 1) offices and the meeting room along the sides of the buildings with a
central hallway 2) the corridors along the perimeters of the building with all offices pulled to the
center and 3) a hybrid of the two with a hallway along the exterior wall on the road side of the
building but offices against the exterior wall on the other side. The meeting space area would
retain the high ceilings and high windows while the office space would not. This seemed to be
the preferred option by the committee at this time, but it did not want to eliminate the first
option.
The committee discussed the merits of the options and touched on topics such as storage, light,
and capacity of the meeting room.
Tim also showed options for the entry from the parking lot to the addition housing the elevator
and staircase. One option shows steps down and a sloped ramp from the parking lot to the
addition door. In this option the floor of the addition is level with the current basement floor.
The other option is to have a level entry from the parking lot meaning the addition floor is
slightly above the current basement level. This would require an additional stop on the elevator
(enter at lobby level and go down to basement or up to first floor) and a couple of inside steps
from the entry lobby down to the basement level. As the drainage in the parking lot is currently
a problem, it was noted that the option chosen must address those drainage issues. The entry that
is level with the parking lot requires an extra elevator stop and double elevator door and is the
more expensive option. Tim shared renderings of the inside of the addition to illustrate it can
look like more than just a lobby with a staircase.
Tim also shared a historic photo of town hall showing that in the past the building was white
with green trim and shutters and he encouraged the committee to think about what the look of the
addition should be.
Discuss public outreach and upcoming Public Information Session.
There was a brief discussion about the presentation to be given by Dan and Tim for the
upcoming public information session. The committee agreed that Mari, Meaghen (P3), and
Melissa (EDM) could approve and send out public outreach materials
Review and approve previous meeting minutes
Mark made a motion, Maggie seconded it, and it was so voted to approve the minutes of
August 18, 2026 as presented.
There being no further business, a motion was made by Maggie, seconded by Mark, and so
voted to adjourn the meeting at 5:24 pm.

This was a virtual meeting as allowed by An Act relative to extending certain COVID-19
measures adopted during the state of emergency, extending certain provisions of the

I. Call to Order & Open Meeting Law Statement
Chair Buck Donovan called the meeting to order at 4:06pm. He stated that BRPC was
recording the meeting and said that if anyone else wanted to record it, they needed to
inform him. Breanna Steele from iBerkshires also recorded the meeting.

Caitlin Davis, Office Administrator, read the roll call.

III. Vote to Approve the minutes of the Executive Committee meeting of July
2, 2026 Minutes
Doug McNally moved to approve the July 2, 2026 meeting minutes. Malcolm Fick
seconded the motion. There was no discussion on the motion.
The motion passed with affirmative votes from: Buck Donovan, Malcolm Fick,
Mark Smith, Kyle Hanlon, Sam Haupt, Mary McGurn and Doug McNally. Sheila
Irvin abstained.
IV. Financial Reports and Discussion
a. Vote to Approve the June 23, 2026 – July 29, 2026, Expenditures Report
Doug McNally moved to approve the June 23, 2026 – July 29, 2026, expenditures
report. Kyle Hanlon seconded the motion. There was no discussion on the
motion.
The motion passed with affirmative votes from: Buck Donovan, Malcolm Fick,
Sheila Irvin, Mark Smith, Kyle Hanlon, Sam Haupt, Mary McGurn and Doug
McNally.
b. Report on the Accounts Receivable July 2026
The Accounts Receivable was in good standing, even with the over 90 day
payments due. Some of the payments listed on the report were already in
process and scheduled. A few over $100k due were receivables have gone
through since the meeting materials were sent out.
c. Report on the Line of Credit – July 2026
The line of credit remained at zero.
V. Open Comments from Berkshire Regional Planning Commission Delegates
and Alternate Delegates not to be further discussed at this meeting by the
Executive Committee.
Mary McGurn commented on the Build in the Berkshires mapping site that was
recently created by BRPC. She was impressed with the site and would like to
share with Egremont’s Planning Board. Laura commented that this was a soft
launch, feedback was welcome, and that it was funded by a FY26 grant from
the MA Executive Office of Energy and Environmental Affairs.
Buck Donovan mentioned Lee’s ribbon cutting ceremony for the housing
development at Eagle Mill, which had been ongoing since 2012. This is an
example of the types of properties displayed on the new website, encouraging
investment.
VI. Update re: Governor’s PILOT Commission-Listening Sessions Update
Sam Haupt gave a brief recap of the July 24th listening session. It was well
2
attended with 100 attendees, including Senator Paul Mark. There were breakout
sessions which were mainly positive. There will be additional sessions conducted
sometime in the fall, once the information and useable data is formatted to
formulate potential modifications to the program. The next sessions would focus
on eligible vs. ineligible lands for reimbursement, as well as the ecological value
and impacts of things such as tourism. Sam would share that information with the
executive committee once it was available. Doug McNally thanked Sam for his
Berkshires representation.
VII. Items Requiring Action
a. Vote to ratify the signing of a contract with Berkshire Community College for the
Northern Berkshire Education Sustainability Study
The Executive Committee was requested to ratify signing by the Executive
Director of agreement with Berkshire Community College, which is the fiduciary
for Berkshire Education Resources K-12 (BERK12), for the Northern Berkshire
Education Sustainability Study. BRPC will provide data and analysis assistance to
the steering committee. The $15,000 contract runs through June 30, 2027. There is
no match required. The staff lead on this project will be Mark Maloy,
mmaloy@berkshireplanning.org , x29.

BUCK DONOVAN, Chair
MALCOLM FICK, Vice-Chair
SHEILA IRVIN, Clerk
LAURA BRENNAN, Executive Director
MEMORANDUM
TO: Delegates and Alternates, Berkshire Regional Planning Commission
FROM: Laura Brennan, Executive Director
DATE: September 10, 2026
SUBJ: Executive Committee Actions taken during the August 6 and September 3, 2026
Meetings
Per the BRPC bylaws, actions taken by the Executive Committee on the Commission's
behalf are reported and presented for discussion at the next Commission meeting.
Executive Committee Actions on September 3, 2026
Approved the minutes of the August 6, 2026 BRPC Executive Committee meeting.
Approved the July 30, 2026 – August 26 2026 Expenditures Report.
Approved the submission of a grant application to the USDA’s Housing Preservation Grant
(HPG) Program
The Executive Committee was requested to authorize the Executive Director to submit a
grant application to the United States Department Agriculture’s Housing Preservation Grant
(HPG) Program and sign any resulting contracts and agreements. This grant would provide
funding for home repair and rehabilitation construction through deferred payment,
forgivable loans for up to 46 very low- and low-income homeowners in West Stockbridge,
Sheffield, Becket, Clarksburg, and New Ashford (communities where we will have active
CDBG Housing Rehabilitation programs, so funding can be paired). Per the Notice of
Funding Opportunity for the HPG, award amounts will be based on the state’s allocation
and number of eligible applicants. Massachusetts’ total allocation is $32,972. Any funds
awarded will leverage Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds in those towns.
There is no match required. BRPC contact is Brett Roberts, broberts@berkshireplanning.org.
Doug McNally moved to approve the Submission of a Grant Application to the USDA’s
Housing Preservation Grant (HPG) Program. Mary McGurn seconded the motion. There was
no discussion on the motion.
The motion passed with affirmative votes from: Buck Donovan, Malcolm Fick, Sheila Irvin,
Mark Smith, Christine Rasmussen, Kyle Hanlon, Mary McGurn and Doug McNally.
Approved the submission of a grant application to the EPA’s Brownfields Job Training
Program
The Executive Committee was requested to authorize the Executive Director to submit a
grant application to the United States Environmental Protection Agency’s Brownfields Job
Training Program and sign any resulting contracts and agreements. This grant would
enable program graduates to obtain skills to secure full-time, sustainable employment in
various aspects of hazardous substances, pollutants, contaminants, and petroleum
products within the larger environmental field, including sustainable remediation, chemical
1 Fenn St., Suite 201, Pittsfield, MA 01201 T: (413) 442-1521 www.berkshireplanning.org
safety, and site preparation for the revitalization of brownfields. Training programs prioritize
unemployed and under-employed residents of communities impacted by a variety of
waste facilities, blighted properties, and contaminated sites. Potential partners include
MassHire Berkshires, Berkshire Community College, McCann Tech, Taconic High School,
and the City of Pittsfield. A final proposed budget is TBD, award ceiling is $300,000 with an
expected 20 awards nationwide. Cost sharing and matching funds are not required nor
permitted under this competition. BRPC contact is Melissa Provencher,
mprovencher@berkshireplanning.org.
Mark Smith moved to approve Submission of a Grant Application to the EPA’s Brownfields
Job Training Program. Doug McNally seconded the motion. There was no discussion on the
motion.
The motion passed with affirmative votes from: Buck Donovan, Malcolm Fick, Sheila Irvin,
Mark Smith, Christine Rasmussen, Kyle Hanlon, Mary McGurn and Doug McNally.
Approved the ratification of the submission (after the fact) of a grant application to the US
Department of Housing and Urban Development’s Older Adults Home Modification Grant
Program
The Executive Committee was requested to authorize the Executive Director to submit a
grant application to the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development’s
Older Adults Home Modification Grant Program and sign any resulting contracts and
agreements. This grant would provide funding for low-cost, high-impact home
modifications for low-income seniors at least 62 years of old throughout Berkshire County.
Per the Notice of Funding Opportunity, 32 awards will be made nation-wide. BRPC will
apply for the minimum award amount of $2 million. Any funds awarded will leverage
Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) and Home Modification Loan Program
(HMLP) funds throughout the county. There is no match required. BRPC contact is Brett
Roberts, broberts@berkshireplanning.org.
Malcolm Fick moved to ratify the Submission (after the fact) of a Grant Application to the
US Department of Housing and Urban Development’s Older Adults Home Modification
Grant Program. Christine Rasmussen seconded the motion. There was no discussion on the
motion.
The motion passed with affirmative votes from: Buck Donovan, Malcolm Fick, Sheila Irvin,
Mark Smith, Christine Rasmussen, Kyle Hanlon, Mary McGurn and Doug McNally.
Approved the ratification of staff comments re: proposed amendments to MassDEP
Waterways Regulations at 310 CMR 9.00
The meeting packet included staff comments submitted prior to the August 20th deadline,
